meta.nieuws.html.description: The latest energy news for hotels: subsidies (EIA, ISDE, SPRILA), EV charging, battery storage, grid congestion and energy costs. Updated daily.
nieuws.intro: Updated daily. Left: general energy news for hotels - subsidies (EIA, ISDE, SPRILA), charging infrastructure, battery storage and grid congestion. Right: hotel-specific news on energy costs and sustainability.
nieuws.s1t: End of SDE subsidy pushes commercial solar panels off roofs early
nieuws.s1p: A growing number of commercial solar installations are reaching the end of their 15-year SDE subsidy period. Research by Copper8 shows that economic pressure makes early removal increasingly attractive, even though the technical lifespan is still 25 years. Important for owners who want to reassess their generation and storage strategy.
nieuws.s2t: South Holland launches action plan for more rooftop solar, subsidy for circular solar panels
nieuws.s2p: The province of South Holland is presenting the Solar Action Plan: 18 measures to reverse the stagnating growth of rooftop solar, including a subsidy for circular solar panels. The plan targets large roofs, facades and parking lots from 15 kWp, directly relevant for hotels with suitable roof space.
nieuws.s3t: Getting a grip on your energy bill in Zeist starts with proper comparison
nieuws.s3p: The energy market remains in flux and commercial customers would do well to compare their contracts critically. De Nieuwsbode offers practical tips for businesses that want to save on energy costs. Also relevant for hoteliers looking for the best deal.
nieuws.s4t: Blocking fee at charging stations may become a thing of the past: EVs should charge longer instead
nieuws.s4p: The common blocking fee charged by charging station providers is under threat. New insights show that EVs actually benefit from staying plugged in longer for grid balancing. For hotels, this could mean a very different revenue model around guests charging overnight.
nieuws.s5t: European EPBD IV directive tightens energy performance requirements for buildings
nieuws.s5p: The new European EPBD IV directive imposes stricter requirements on the energy performance of utility buildings, including hotels. RVO explains what the new rules mean for building owners and which steps you can already take towards compliance.
nieuws.s6t: Rising energy prices drive up commuting costs: will employers compensate?
nieuws.s6p: Higher electricity and fuel prices are also pushing up staff mobility costs. AutoGids investigates whether employers should compensate these costs. Directly relevant for hotels that provide charging infrastructure for both staff and guests.
nieuws.s7t: Going on holiday with an EV? Beware of extreme charging rates: €500 per charging session
nieuws.s7p: Motorists taking an electric car on holiday risk sky-high charging costs. In extreme cases this can be as much as €500 per charging session. Autovisie warns about the proliferation of expensive roaming rates and offers tips to avoid them.
nieuws.s8t: Zytec saves a lot of power with contactless magnetic coupling for pumps
nieuws.s8p: Zytec equips industrial pumps with a contactless magnetic coupling, saving a significant amount of power. It shows how targeted technical innovation reduces energy consumption without sacrificing capacity.
nieuws.s9t: Negative energy prices in Belgium: prosumers must become true flexumers
nieuws.s9p: Negative electricity prices are increasingly common in Belgium. The lesson for companies with their own generation: move from pure consumer to flexumer, steering on price moments. Battery storage is the final piece of that puzzle.
nieuws.s10t: EPBD-III mandates charging infrastructure at utility buildings, also for hotels
nieuws.s10p: The EPBD-III directive requires charging infrastructure in new builds and large-scale renovations of utility buildings. For hotels with parking facilities this means concrete charging point standards. RVO outlines what already applies and what will be added in the coming years.
nieuws.s11t: Recycling Li-ion batteries in the Netherlands: big ambitions, small volumes
nieuws.s11p: The Dutch battery recycling market is still in its infancy. Duurzaam Ondernemen outlines the gap between ambitious policy goals and the reality of small processing volumes. Ahead of stricter EU rules, the urgency for a mature recycling chain is growing.
nieuws.s12t: German government allocates billions in energy support for businesses
nieuws.s12p: Germany is spending billions to compensate residents and businesses for high energy costs. A sign that our eastern neighbours take the energy bill seriously, a development Dutch entrepreneurs are also following closely.
nieuws.s13t: Net metering scheme ends in 2027: parliament pushes for bidirectional charging
nieuws.s13p: The Senate has approved phasing out the net metering scheme from 2027. At the same time, politics is opting to stimulate bidirectional charging as a smart successor. That technology unlocks extra revenue potential for hotels with solar panels and chargers.

nieuws.h1t: Entrepreneurs in Oss store power in a megabattery, freeing up space on the congested grid
nieuws.h1p: Entrepreneurs in Oss are using a megabattery to collectively tackle grid congestion. By storing power locally they free up space on the overloaded power grid. A textbook example of how business parks and hotels can take matters into their own hands.
nieuws.h2t: Hospitality entrepreneurs bypass the full power grid with their own battery storage
nieuws.h2p: More and more hospitality and hotel entrepreneurs are taking matters into their own hands, investing in their own battery storage to bypass the effects of grid congestion. Entree Magazine describes how entrepreneurs creatively respond to an overloaded power grid. A trend the hotel industry is embracing ever faster.
nieuws.h3t: EPBD mandates charging infrastructure at utility buildings, including hotels
nieuws.h3p: The revised European EPBD directive sets strict requirements for charging infrastructure at utility buildings, including hotels with parking facilities. RVO explains which obligations are coming and what hoteliers can already do to prepare.
nieuws.h4t: No grid connection, but a McDonald's entrepreneur found a solution: look at what is possible
nieuws.h4p: A McDonald's entrepreneur without a grid connection shows what is possible: getting started anyway with an energy hub and smart storage. An inspiring example for hoteliers who cannot get a connection.
nieuws.h5t: Full power grid causes frustration: how do you deal with it as a hospitality business?
nieuws.h5p: Entree Magazine investigates how hospitality and hotel entrepreneurs deal with the reality of an overloaded power grid. The sector is finding increasingly creative ways to keep operating despite grid congestion, from battery storage to smart charging solutions.
nieuws.h6t: Entrepreneurs find creative ways out of years-long power grid waiting lists
nieuws.h6p: Frustration over the endless waiting lists for a grid connection is making way for creativity. De Telegraaf profiles entrepreneurs who get started anyway with battery storage and energy hubs. An example for hoteliers who cannot get a connection.

nieuws.n1t: Qurmit launches four new batteries with storage capacity up to 101 kWh
nieuws.n1p: Dutch manufacturer Qurmit is bringing four new models to market with storage capacities ranging from 57 to 101 kWh. The lead-gel batteries are non-flammable and therefore fall outside the PGS 37 safety rules, an interesting option for hotels looking to bypass grid congestion without heavy fire-safety requirements.
nieuws.n2t: Energy company must repay hidden feed-in costs to solar panel owner
nieuws.n2p: The Energy Disputes Commission ruled that feed-in costs buried in the fine print are not legally valid. An energy company must repay the costs. For hotels with solar panels, a signal to review their contract for unfair feed-in costs.
nieuws.n3t: Solar panels cover 10 percent of global electricity demand for the first time
nieuws.n3p: In the first half of 2026, solar energy supplied a record 10 percent of all electricity worldwide. Think tank Ember concludes that batteries make it possible to use that solar energy beyond sunlight hours, exactly the combination hotels with their own generation benefit from.
nieuws.n4t: Energy sector calls for a strong National Investment Institution
nieuws.n4p: A broad coalition of energy and climate organisations is urging the Taskforce Toekomstige Welvaart to focus the planned National Investment Institution on energy, climate and the circular economy. More public capital could accelerate the financing of sustainability for businesses and real estate.
nieuws.n5t: Belgian regulator definitively scraps grid-fee exemption for large batteries
nieuws.n5p: Belgian energy regulator CREG is definitively phasing out the grid-fee exemption for large-scale battery storage; existing projects remain protected under conditions. A signal for the Dutch market on the direction grid fees for batteries are heading.
nieuws.n6t: Plug-in home battery: a great product, but a lack of rules
nieuws.n6p: The rise of the plug-in battery (plugged into a wall socket) raises questions about safety and grid management. Industry association Techlink calls for clear rules. Relevant for businesses looking for a low-threshold start with energy storage.

nieuws.h7t: Construction of Van der Valk hotel delayed by power shortage
nieuws.h7p: Construction of a new Van der Valk hotel is being delayed by a shortage of grid capacity. A concrete example of how grid congestion also affects new-build hospitality - and why energy independence is becoming increasingly important for hotels.
nieuws.u1t: Alfen revenue grows almost a quarter thanks to batteries and smart grids
nieuws.u1p: Alfen posted revenue growth of 23.6 percent in the first half of 2026, to €261.5 million. Growth in energy storage and smart grids compensates for the declining sale of chargers, a sign that battery storage for businesses is maturing.
nieuws.u2t: EcoFlow launches STREAM AC 5000 home battery for existing solar panels
nieuws.u2p: EcoFlow is bringing the AC-coupled home battery STREAM AC 5000 to the Netherlands, designed to be added to existing solar panel installations. The system works with the current inverter and P1 meter, without major conversion.
nieuws.u3t: Energy storage sector raises nearly $9 billion in first half of 2026
nieuws.u3p: Companies in the energy storage sector raised $8.9 billion in capital worldwide in the first six months of 2026, according to Mercom Capital Group. It underlines the momentum behind battery storage as the core of the energy transition.
nieuws.u4t: Cabinet allocates €197 million to municipalities around new substations
nieuws.u4p: Municipalities around high-voltage grid expansions can claim nearly €197 million for quality of life and environmental measures. Applications open from 15 October; first payments follow in early 2027.
nieuws.u5t: Smart charging makes electric driving almost 7 times cheaper than petrol
nieuws.u5p: Tibber customers paid an average of €2.76 per 100 kilometres in July thanks to smart charging, compared with €18.30 for petrol; some could even charge for free. For hotels, it shows how smart load management turns charging into a cost advantage.
nieuws.u6t: State Secretary De Bat: Tilburg power outage says nothing about the grid
nieuws.u6p: The recent power outage in Tilburg is no proof that grid congestion threatens the reliability of existing connections, State Secretary De Bat said in answers to parliament. The outage was caused by a local technical fault, not by congestion.
nieuws.h8t: Stop communicating labels; show real verifiable sustainability data
nieuws.h8p: The hospitality sector stands at a turning point: what started as simple energy and water savings has grown into a forest of sustainability labels, ESG requirements and stricter regulation. Hospitality Management argues for stopping the communication of labels and instead showing real, verifiable sustainability data.
nieuws.s14t: Austria shifts subsidies after hot summer from solar panels to batteries
nieuws.s14p: The extremely sunny summer of 2026 has turned Austrian subsidy policy on its head: from next year the focus shifts from solar panels to battery storage. During the day solar power in the Alpine country is extremely cheap, while prices explode in the evening, exactly the peak-off-peak problem that Dutch hotels with solar on their roof also face.
nieuws.s15t: Hanoi wants subsidies of up to 6 million dong for solar panels on household roofs
nieuws.t1p: A company from the Hoeksche Waard is one of the first in the Netherlands to distribute available power more smartly, relieving the overcrowded power grid. Grid operator Stedin is enthusiastic and sees opportunities to deploy the approach on a much larger scale.
nieuws.t1t: Company from Hoeksche Waard among the first in the Netherlands to apply a new solution to an overcrowded power grid
nieuws.t2p: TU Delft researchers conclude that a battery for an energy community is only financially viable if it also provides grid services; buying cheap power alone is not enough. Their energy management system was tested in a distribution grid with homes and business premises. A relevant outcome for hotels that want to store collectively.
nieuws.t2t: TU Delft: battery for an energy community only profitable when providing grid services
nieuws.t3p: If it is up to the cabinet, every new car must be able to charge bidirectionally by 2035. Robin Berg of We Drive Solar thinks that is feasible, provided a few stubborn bottlenecks are solved. A development for hotels to follow, because charging thus becomes a revenue model instead of a cost.
nieuws.t3t: When will bidirectional charging become the standard for electric cars?
nieuws.v1p: The Scientific Council for Government Policy (WRR) warns that Europe is becoming dangerously dependent on China for solar panels, batteries and wind turbines, and that this dependence is growing. Only a different trade and industrial policy can reverse this trend, according to advice that could also affect the Dutch battery market.
nieuws.v1t: Advisory council: with every Chinese battery Europe buys dependence, change course
nieuws.v2p: Danish energy provider Emaldo connects its commercial batteries to the Dutch Eddy Grid platform. Smart algorithms give battery customers access to multiple electricity markets at once. This makes storage an active instrument against high peak rates for businesses too.
nieuws.v2t: Emaldo connects commercial batteries to the Eddy Grid platform
nieuws.v3p: Almost a third of the subsidies for home sustainability improvements in recent years went to households with an income above 100,000 euros, minister Van Veldhoven admitted in answer to parliamentary questions. The cabinet is examining how the money can be targeted more effectively; a signal that subsidy conditions may be tightened.

nieuws.s16p: The Dutch consumer and market authority (ACM) concludes that the planned legislative change around feed-in costs offers insufficient transparency and calls for a mandatory price per kilowatt hour. For hotels with solar panels this means more clarity about what feeding back will cost, and why smart self-consumption pays off.
nieuws.s16t: Watchdog: mandatory feed-in cost per kilowatt hour to give solar panel owners clarity
nieuws.s17p: Grid-conscious new builds enable 180 to 430 additional homes per district on an overloaded power grid, according to research by CE Delft commissioned by provinces, grid operators and the cabinet. The principle of building smarter instead of waiting for grid expansion also helps utility construction and businesses.
nieuws.s17t: Full power grid? Grid-conscious building straightforwardly solves the housing problem
nieuws.s18t: Gigabattery of 800 megawatt hours for Groningen: Vattenfall and Return sign historic deal
nieuws.x1p: At the request of the Ministry of Climate and Green Growth, CBS publishes monthly overviews of the distribution of energy tariffs. The seventh edition, with figures up to and including July 2026, is online. A handy reference for hoteliers reviewing their energy contract.
nieuws.x1t: CBS maps the spread of 2026 energy tariffs monthly
nieuws.x2p: At EnergyHub Branderwal in Kootwijkerbroek a 20 MW, 80 MWh battery has been taken into use. The battery relieves the loaded electricity grid and ensures sixty businesses at the Harselaar-Zuid business park still get a connection, a textbook example of how storage creates room on a tight power grid.
nieuws.x2t: Battery at EnergyHub Branderwal helps 60 businesses get a power connection
nieuws.s19t: Consumentenbond: heat pump subsidy should also impose quality requirements on installers
nieuws.s19p: The Dutch Consumers' Association wants the ISDE subsidy to impose quality requirements not only on the heat pump itself, but also on the company installing it. The scheme currently has no installer requirements at all, while distrust of contractors often makes consumers hesitate to go green.
nieuws.s20t: Need power for a new home? This is how you get to the top of the connection list in Nijmegen
nieuws.s21t: Explosive growth of 8.6 gigawatts predicted: the Netherlands is getting dozens of new battery parks
nieuws.s21p: Battery parks in the Netherlands are growing fast: dozens of new parks are expected, together adding 8.6 gigawatts of capacity. More large-scale storage relieves the congested grid and dampens price spikes — also for hotels that cannot get a heavier connection due to grid congestion.
nieuws.s22t: Tackling grid congestion: water authority wants to save power by 'smart pumping'
nieuws.s22p: A Dutch water authority wants to fight grid congestion by 'smart pumping': pumping stations only run when the grid has spare capacity. Another example of flexible energy use — the same logic hotels can apply with a battery and energy management.
nieuws.y1t: Almost 20 percent of Dutch electricity comes from solar: sector prepares for next growth phase
nieuws.y1p: Solar power supplied almost 20 percent of all Dutch electricity in 2025. The build-out of new panels is levelling off, but Holland Solar sees a next growth phase towards 2040 — with more solar plus smart storage to put the supply to use.
nieuws.y2t: Negative power prices increasingly make solar parks unprofitable despite subsidy
nieuws.y2p: In 2025, solar parks missed SDE++ subsidy on 24 percent of their potential output because negative power prices block payouts — up from 3 percent in 2021. The more often prices dive below zero, the more self-consumption and battery storage determine whether a solar roof still pays off.
nieuws.y3t: Gas bill could explode towards 2050: ACM warns about those left behind on the gas grid
nieuws.y3p: Anyone still dependent on natural gas in 2050 will likely pay four times as much for gas transport as today, according to new ACM estimates. The more users leave the gas grid, the more expensive the network becomes for those who stay — a strong reason to review the gas connection now.
nieuws.y4t: Energy cooperatives demand a fair queue for the power grid: money must no longer decide who goes first
nieuws.y4p: As the cabinet rushes grid congestion legislation, umbrella organisation Energie Samen also wants a fairer queue for grid capacity: a project's maturity — for example via a maturity test — should decide who goes first, not its wallet.
nieuws.y5t: Construction of Amsterdam's largest-ever power station starts where coal used to be burned
nieuws.y5p: Grid operators Liander and TenneT have started building the Nieuwe Hemweg substation: the largest expansion of Amsterdam's grid ever, with around 1 gigawatt of capacity. The station on the old coal plant site will supply thousands of homes and businesses.
nieuws.y6t: Cabinet admits AI data centres threaten the energy transition but won't ban them: national approach coming
nieuws.y6p: State Secretary Aerdts admits that buying green power does not automatically make a data centre good for the energy system and announces a national approach this autumn. Data centres increasingly compete with other large users for scarce grid capacity.
nieuws.y7t: China halts approvals for new battery factories over looming overcapacity
nieuws.y7p: China has temporarily frozen all approvals for new factories producing battery cells for energy storage, citing fears of overcapacity in the fast-growing storage sector. The move could slow the rapid global price decline of batteries and strengthens the European call for own production.
nieuws.z1t: Subsidy scheme for energy hubs opens: businesses working together can receive up to €42,000
nieuws.z1p: From 1 October, businesses can apply for the new RVO scheme Research Energy Hubs (EHUB). A total of €9.6 million is available; businesses working together can receive up to €42,000 for a feasibility study into an energy hub.
nieuws.z2t: Policy agencies: relaxing EU climate rules barely lowers energy costs
nieuws.z2p: CPB and PBL analysed the EU plans to soften carbon pricing for businesses. Their conclusion: it mainly costs climate gains, while business energy costs barely fall.
nieuws.z3t: Business electric driving in 2026 and 2027: facts and myths
nieuws.z3p: What is true about all the stories on electric driving for entrepreneurs? De Zaak lists the facts, myths and rules for 2026 and 2027 — from addition to charging costs. Also useful for hotels that want to align their fleet policy and charging infrastructure.
nieuws.z4t: Home battery becomes a money-maker: savings rise 40 percent by 2030
nieuws.z4p: CE Delft calculates that a battery will save around 40 percent more on the energy bill in 2030 than today. With the time-dependent grid tariff, shifting your own consumption becomes more lucrative than trading on the energy market - a development that will matter for hotels with their own generation too.
nieuws.z5t: Solar panels become more attractive again after the end of net metering, CE Delft concludes
nieuws.z5p: Even without net metering, solar panels cut the energy bill by 350 to 500 euros per year in 2030, about 20 percent more than now. The new time-dependent grid tariff rewards self-consumption, so rooftop solar becomes more attractive, not less.
nieuws.z6t: Energy prices surge on Iran war and empty gas stocks, consumers sign longer contracts more often
nieuws.z6p: Geopolitical unrest and low gas stocks are driving energy prices up. Five times as many households as in January are now choosing a multi-year contract; a three-year contract is on average about 190 euros cheaper than a one-year deal. For businesses this is a moment to review their own contract.
nieuws.z7t: Manufacturers of inverters, batteries and charging stations must report exploited vulnerabilities from 11 September
nieuws.z7p: From 11 September, manufacturers of inverters, batteries, EV chargers, EMS and smart meter gateways must report actively exploited vulnerabilities to the Dutch NCSC. Security updates are mandatory for at least five years - relevant for every installation hotels rely on.
nieuws.z8t: ACM cannot guarantee that contested feed-in tariff will save the Netherlands money
nieuws.z8p: During a technical briefing, the ACM admitted it cannot guarantee that the contested producer tariff lowers total social costs. Large connections above 3x80 amps will start paying; small consumers with a home battery remain out of scope for now.
nieuws.z9t: Budget Day: scrapping VAT on home batteries costs the government 1 to 2 billion euros
nieuws.z9p: If The Hague scrapped VAT on batteries from 1 January 2027, it would cost over 365 million euros next year alone and nearly 1.5 billion within five years. The end of net metering makes storage more attractive: researchers estimate new storage capacity of 4.5 gigawatt hours for 2027.
nieuws.h9t: 30-day limit can affect hotels' longstay offering
nieuws.h9p: KHN responds to the proposed 'Suitable rental contracts' bill. The proposed 30-day limit could seriously affect hotels' longstay and extended-stay formats; KHN is asking the cabinet for exemptions for the hotel sector.
nieuws.h10t: Subsidy for a cyber-resilient hospitality business
nieuws.h10p: With the My Cyber-Resilient Business scheme you get 50 percent of the costs of digital security measures reimbursed, up to a maximum of 1,250 euros. Intended for sole traders and small businesses with up to 50 employees - useful for hospitality businesses and small hotels.
nieuws.q1t: Depraetere cuts subsidies for large solar parks: everyone's power bill drops a little
nieuws.q1p: The Flemish government is scaling back support for large solar installations: green certificates will now be withdrawn after fifteen minutes of negative power prices instead of after six hours. Flemish energy minister Melissa Depraetere frees up 179 million euros on the electricity bill and expects large installations to shut down or store power faster, reducing the surplus on the grid. Scrapping the subsidy altogether is not allowed under European rules.
nieuws.q3t: Solar energy grew more slowly again in the Netherlands in 2025
nieuws.q3p: Installed solar capacity rose to 29.4 gigawatt-peak in 2025 and solar power accounted for 19.7 percent of Dutch electricity production. Yet only 1.4 GWp was added last year, against 3.3 GWp in 2024 and 5.2 GWp in 2023. Uncertainty about returns, an overloaded grid, more hours of negative prices and the end of net metering are holding growth back: RVO expects an average of 1.3 GWp per year until 2028.
nieuws.q4t: CBS publishes eighth monthly table on the spread of 2026 energy tariffs
nieuws.q4p: At the request of the Ministry of Climate Policy and Green Growth, CBS maps the spread of energy tariffs every month. The eighth table of 2026 shows how electricity and gas tariffs developed from January through August - useful for benchmarking your own contract or tender.
nieuws.q5t: New KHN chairman puts burden reduction at the top of the agenda
nieuws.q5p: Ralf Benda became chairman of Koninklijke Horeca Nederland on 1 September and immediately pushed an economic agenda towards politics ahead of Budget Day: lower burdens and more room to do business. KHN points to the stacking of staff costs, energy costs, the VAT increase on accommodation from 9 to 21 percent, local levies and regulatory pressure. With thirty years of experience in international hotels and hospitality, Benda makes burden reduction the key lobbying theme of his chairmanship.
nieuws.b1t: PBL: lack of CO2-free flexibility is the biggest bottleneck for the power sector up to 2040, more batteries needed
nieuws.b1p: According to the Climate and Energy Outlook 2026, it is not the price of solar panels but the oversupply on sunny afternoons that holds back further growth: PBL calls the lack of CO2-free flexibility the biggest bottleneck for the electricity sector up to 2040. Batteries must ensure that a larger share of that production is actually used, although stand-alone battery projects themselves also run into the queue for a grid connection.
nieuws.b2t: Households will pay much more to transport electricity next year: grid costs rise by 141 euros
nieuws.b2p: ACM reports that households will pay on average 89 euros more in 2027 to transport electricity and 52 euros more for gas, mainly because of policy choices and investments in an overloaded grid. Grid congestion costs society an estimated 10 to 40 billion euros a year, as companies cannot expand and housing construction is delayed.
nieuws.b3t: Two-way contracts good for 7 gigawatts of extra solar panels
nieuws.b3p: With two-way contracts, installed solar capacity in 2040 could reach around 53 gigawatts instead of 46 gigawatts, according to the Climate and Energy Outlook 2026 by PBL. From 2027, onshore wind and solar can no longer be supported through the classic SDE++ scheme; the Netherlands will switch to two-way contracts.
nieuws.b4t: Power grid vulnerable to hackers: stricter cybersecurity requirements for batteries, charging stations and solar panels
nieuws.b4p: Answering parliamentary questions, Minister Van Veldhoven confirms that solar panels, batteries and charging stations increase the attack surface for hackers. The Cyber Security Act has been in force since mid-August and the European Network Code for Cybersecurity becomes fully effective in 2028; the RDI supervises compliance and digital resilience is a responsibility of the entire chain, according to the ministry.
nieuws.b5t: After 2.5 years of construction, a new substation near Schiphol brings relief to the overloaded grid
nieuws.b5p: TenneT and Liander commissioned the Rozenburg-Zuid station near Schiphol, increasing power capacity in the Haarlemmermeer region and helping companies waiting for a heavier connection more quickly. Because of a lack of space the station is built indoors with a special insulating gas; a structural solution for the waiting list still requires many more grid expansions.
nieuws.b6t: Electric truck that also works as a battery: Rent a Battery brings world first to market
nieuws.b6p: Rent a Battery from Schiedam introduces the Puma Powertruck: the world's first electric truck that doubles as a mobile 1 megawatt-hour battery and delivers up to 200 kilowatts on site for five hours. For hotels and event venues that means temporary power without a diesel generator or an extra grid connection.
nieuws.b7t: The Netherlands misses European renewable energy target and will even import power in 2030
nieuws.hn1p: In a round-table discussion on hotel real estate and financing, BWH Hotels, Foruminvest and ABN AMRO say sustainability has become mainly a return-on-investment issue: energy labels and smart building management systems now weigh on a hotel's financeability. In their view it only works if it is practically applicable in operations and noticeably improves guest comfort.
nieuws.hn2t: Hotel industry still performs strongly in 2025, but margins come under further pressure
nieuws.hn2p: The HOSTA 2026 figures from Horwath HTL and ABN AMRO show an occupancy rate of 76.5 percent, but also a lower average room rate and a further declining operating margin. The VAT increase on accommodation, ongoing cost rises and higher tourist taxes put extra pressure on the sector, says KHN chairman Ralf Benda.
nieuws.hn3t: Paying for two years of sick leave? Employers are fed up
nieuws.hn3p: KHN chairman Ralf Benda writes about the stacking of employer costs, with continued wage payments during long-term illness as the biggest worry for SME hospitality entrepreneurs. The Netherlands differs from countries such as Germany and Belgium, where financial responsibility lies with collective schemes much earlier.
nieuws.hn4t: KHN Aa en Hunze/Borger-Odoorn critical of tourist tax
nieuws.hn4p: The municipal council of Borger-Odoorn raises the tourist tax for hotels from 1.75 to 2.50 euros per overnight stay from 2027, while campsites and group accommodation are taxed less heavily. KHN objected together with HISWA-RECRON and is in talks with the municipality about the consequences for the accommodation sector.
nieuws.hn5t: Van der Valk hotel writes urgent letter after sharp tourist tax increase
nieuws.hn5p: Van der Valk Hotel Almere opposes the municipality's plan to raise the tourist tax from 7 to 10 euros per overnight stay, an increase of more than 40 percent. The hotel points to the combination with the higher VAT rate on accommodation, fears a competitive disadvantage compared with neighbouring municipalities and is considering legal advice.
nieuws.e1t: Cabinet anchors increase of Energy Investment Allowance in Tax Plan: deduction rate rises from 40 to 45.5 percent
nieuws.e1p: From 1 January 2027 entrepreneurs who invest in energy-saving business assets may deduct a larger share of that investment from taxable profit: the EIA rate rises from 40 to 45.5 percent. The cabinet is laying this down definitively in the Tax Plan 2027. Last year businesses invested a record 1 billion euros in batteries with EIA support, and batteries and charging stations are on the approved list of business assets.
nieuws.e2t: Nearly half a billion for ISDE in 2027, but the budget shrinks sharply in the years after
nieuws.e2p: For 2027 the cabinet budgets almost 499 million euros for the ISDE scheme, roughly the same amount as this year. Looking further ahead the budget falls sharply: to 473 million euros in 2028, 420 million in 2029 and 347 million in 2030. From 2027 stricter requirements for smart control will apply to heat pumps, a direct response to grid congestion.
nieuws.e3t: Cabinet frees up money for batteries at businesses hit by grid congestion when greening their mobility
nieuws.e3p: The budget of the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management makes funds available for businesses blocked by grid congestion when greening and electrifying their mobility. Batteries and tailored advice are explicitly named as mitigating measures, and an advice desk for entrepreneurs in that position is being set up at RVO. A concrete budget and the type of instrument, grant or loan, are not yet mentioned.
nieuws.e4t: Cheaper power in off-peak hours: cabinet embraces time-dependent grid tariff as a weapon against rising energy costs
nieuws.e4p: The cabinet sees cheaper off-peak power as a policy instrument rather than a technical detail: in the Budget Day letter minister Van Veldhoven writes that a lower off-peak tariff gives households more control over their energy bill. Grid operators asked the ACM to introduce the time-dependent grid tariff on 1 January 2029 for households and small business connections. For hotels this makes shifting consumption and charging to quiet hours more attractive.
nieuws.e5t: Cabinet targets 110 gigawatt hours of batteries and at most 95 gigawatt-peak of solar panels in 2040
nieuws.e5p: The updated National Energy System Plan contains a national target for battery storage for the first time: 110 gigawatt hours in 2040, equal to 28 gigawatts of power and an average storage duration of about four hours. For solar panels the cabinet lowers the ambition to 75 to 95 gigawatt-peak in 2040. The Netherlands currently has around 30 gigawatt-peak, meaning 3 to over 4.5 gigawatt-peak must be added every year until 2040.
nieuws.e6t: Grid operators welcome first crisis measures for the overloaded power grid, but urge the cabinet to move faster
nieuws.e6p: Netbeheer Nederland welcomes the legislative package with which the cabinet tackles the grid congestion crisis, but wants measures for the medium and low-voltage grid added as well. State Secretary De Bat announced that unnecessary appeal and objection procedures will be shortened and that part of the reserve capacity on the grid will be released, so homes, schools and businesses get a connection sooner. Thousands of businesses are still on the waiting list for a new or heavier connection.
nieuws.e7t: TNO forecast: average energy bill 120 euros a year higher in 2031
nieuws.e7p: TNO expects the average annual energy bill of Dutch households to rise from about 2020 euros in 2026 to 2140 euros in 2031. Higher grid costs and new costs for emissions trading, green gas blending and the end of net metering outweigh the fall in gas consumption. Not yet included is that the end of net metering may actually trigger more self-consumption through home batteries.
nieuws.hn6t: SME Sprint subsidy 2026-2027 available for entrepreneurs in Limburg
nieuws.hn6p: SME entrepreneurs in Limburg can apply for a Sprint subsidy from 21 September to 21 October 2026 for digitalisation, sustainability, circularity or labour productivity. The scheme covers up to 50 percent of eligible project costs, with a minimum of 5,000 and a maximum of 24,500 euros per company. It is also interesting for hospitality entrepreneurs investing in energy efficiency; two more application rounds follow in 2027.
nieuws.hn7t: KHN Amsterdam chairman shares his view on tourism policy: ‘Amsterdam drives away the wrong visitor’
nieuws.hn7p: KHN Amsterdam chairman Pim Evers argues in an interview with Het Parool for a different view of the visitor economy in the capital. In his view Amsterdam risks losing exactly those visitors who spend a lot and cause relatively little nuisance, while hospitality, culture and shops live off that spending. He wants policy to look not only at visitor numbers but also at the economic and social value.
nieuws.e8t: Cabinet postpones extra climate measures until spring 2027, Council of State demands action now
nieuws.e8p: The Netherlands is not meeting its climate targets, but the cabinet wants to take decisions on additional measures only in the spring 2027 budget round. The advisory division of the Council of State demands action now in its 2026 Climate Review: the 2030 target is far out of reach and so is the European contribution to the 2040 goal of 90 percent emission reduction. Minister Van Veldhoven sticks to the commitment towards 2030, 2040 and 2050, with an eye on affordability.
nieuws.e9t: CE Delft: charging station, home battery and heat pump almost always fit within a single-phase connection
nieuws.e9p: A heat pump, electric car or battery fits within the existing connection in most cases, as long as it is controlled smartly; only a heat pump and a car together become tight, CE Delft concludes. It is not the capacity of the individual devices that determines how much connection capacity you need, but how often they draw power simultaneously. An energy management system that aligns charger, heat pump and battery keeps the peak below the limit - exactly why steering is the first step and a heavier connection the last.
nieuws.f1t: Climate Fund pumps money into Flex-E subsidy for batteries at businesses
nieuws.f1p: The cabinet is topping up the Flex-E subsidy scheme with money from the Climate and Energy Fund: 36.6 million euros is available in 2027 and 2028 for businesses that use batteries to make their power use more flexible. Companies with a large-consumer connection in a congestion area can apply for a flexibility scan, a feasibility study or an investment subsidy; the subsidy rate is 40 percent with a maximum of 300,000 euros per application. Grid operators asked for a scale-up to 125 million euros a year, but were turned down.
nieuws.f2t: End of net metering: SP forces parliamentary debate on higher energy bills for tenants and sports clubs
nieuws.f2p: Scrapping the net metering scheme hits sports clubs, community centres and social housing tenants hard: sports clubs pay on average 6,500 euros more per year, tenants 25 to 50 euros per month. SP MP Jimmy Dijk gathered thirty members behind a dedicated debate with minister Van Veldhoven, to be held within two months. For hotels with their own generation it underlines how important self-consumption and storage become now that feeding back pays less.
nieuws.f3t: Dutch problem of failing inverters almost gone, all arrows on grid congestion
nieuws.f3p: While Flemish solar owners are compensated when their inverter fails, the Netherlands focuses on structural grid improvements. According to Enexis manager Thijs Derksen this is no longer a large-scale national phenomenon: fault reports at Enexis fell from 1,400 in 2023 to 1,000 in 2025 and less than 5 percent of low-voltage faults are still caused by overloading. The big dossier now is the crowded grid, not the individual inverter.
nieuws.f4t: Cabinet expects electricity share of energy use to rise to 50 percent in 2040
nieuws.f4p: In the updated National Energy System Plan the cabinet assumes electricity will cover half of Dutch energy use by 2040, against roughly a quarter today. Domestic electricity demand must more than double from around 105 to 260 terawatt hours, with the strongest growth in industry, mobility and data centres. The cabinet acknowledges that grid congestion will slow that growth until 2035, but sticks to electrification as the preferred route.
nieuws.f5t: Dutch fire service: ‘the plug-in home battery is our problem child’
nieuws.f5p: Do not place a battery in an escape route, put it on its own circuit with fire-resistant cladding and arrange early smoke detection plus flue gas extraction: with those simple measures 80 percent of the risks are gone, according to the fire service. The plug-in battery is the main worry, because user behaviour is hard to control. Practical guidance for hotels installing battery storage or charging infrastructure.
nieuws.f6t: The solar panel emergency button: necessary safety valve or lack of trust?
nieuws.f6p: Grid operators Elia and TenneT are open to an emergency button that temporarily switches off solar panels when the grid is extremely busy, though for different reasons: Belgium struggles with grid frequency, the Netherlands with congestion. Both point to the same gap: too few users shift consumption to moments of surplus, partly because dynamic tariffs are barely chosen.
nieuws.f7t: Von der Leyen: Europe’s future is electric, but that demands swift action on crowded grids
nieuws.f7p: In her State of the Union, Commission President Von der Leyen makes electrification a spearhead: six times more capacity than the 80 gigawatts Europe installed last year is still waiting for a grid connection, and the Netherlands leads in waiting times with periods of up to ten years. She names energy storage explicitly alongside grid expansion. Brussels is working on first-ready-first-served and much shorter permit procedures.
nieuws.f8t: Budget Day 2026: what the plans mean for your hospitality business
nieuws.f8p: KHN lists the Budget Memorandum and Tax Plan, and the conclusion is hardly surprising: the burden keeps stacking up. The ceiling on the tax on drinking water disappears and the levy rises by 10 cents per cubic metre, almost 23 percent; a city hotel with 40 rooms goes from around 129 euros of water tax in 2025 to roughly 3,200 euros in 2027. On the positive side are the larger discretionary margin in the work-related costs scheme and the postponement of the shortening of the unemployment benefit period, while energy savings and financing stay on the sustainability agenda.
nieuws.g1t: Research launched into merging Energy Investment Allowance and Environmental Investment Allowance
nieuws.g1p: The cabinet is investigating whether the Energy Investment Allowance (EIA), the Environmental Investment Allowance (MIA) and the Vamil can be merged into one new robust tax scheme for sustainable investments, as laid down in the coalition agreement. No decision has been taken yet, but regardless of the outcome the EIA deduction rate will rise from 40 to 45.5 percent on 1 January 2027 – also for investments in batteries. An earlier study warned that administrative costs could increase sharply in the event of a fundamental change.
nieuws.g2t: Enexis grid full: 85,000 new homes on the waiting list
nieuws.g2p: Grid operator Enexis is putting more than 85,000 new-build homes on its waiting list because there is no room on the electricity grid. Of the 140,000-plus homes submitted by municipalities and developers under the national transition scheme, direct capacity can be reserved for only about 54,000 – under 40 percent. Normally Enexis connects around 25,000 homes a year; the pressure is greatest in Noord-Brabant. Grid capacity thus remains the deciding factor for hotels and their expansion plans too.
nieuws.g3t: The battle for power now starts at town hall: what does the ‘Apply earlier’ scheme solve?
nieuws.s23t: Two-thirds of SPriLa subsidy applicants choose a stationary battery
nieuws.s23p: Two-thirds of the companies applying for SPriLa subsidy for private charging infrastructure this year combine it with a stationary battery. That emerges from a letter to parliament by state secretary Annet Bertram: the sub-budget for battery storage was oversubscribed almost immediately. The total budget has been raised by 35 million euros from the heavy goods vehicle levy to 122.5 million euros, and the scheme stays open until 18 December. Batteries flatten peaks in power draw, which lets charging infrastructure go ahead even on congested grids.
nieuws.s24t: 40 million for SME sustainability, 80 million for energy fixers
nieuws.s24p: The 2027 budget reserves 40.8 million euros for the Energiebesparing MKB scheme. Businesses that struggle to obtain external financing can use it to take out a loan for energy-saving measures; the scheme opens in 2026 and the first payouts follow in 2027, with 11 million in 2028 and 5.8 million in 2029. In addition, 80 million euros is set aside for the Energiefixers programme and the SVVE owners association subsidy receives 25 million euros extra.
nieuws.s25t: Brabant grid under threat in 9 places: government and province step in with crisis team
nieuws.s25p: In nine locations in Noord-Brabant, electricity demand exceeds available grid capacity at peak moments, putting security of supply and safety at risk. The national government, the province, the Brabant energy regions, grid operators Enexis and TenneT and regulator ACM are working out concrete measures over the next twelve months in a Netcongestie Brabant administrative consultation. The starting point is not the longest waiting lists but the greatest grid risks; scarce capacity is allocated through ACM’s prioritisation framework, which gives precedence to projects of major public interest.
nieuws.s26t: Sustainable frontrunners in hospitality honoured at Gastvrij Rotterdam
nieuws.s26p: The Gaia Green Awards 2026 were presented during Gastvrij Rotterdam to leading sustainable hotels, restaurants and MICE venues. Stayokay Amsterdam Stadsdoelen won in the Hotels category: a gas-free renovated monument from 1730 with a heat pump and on-site energy generation. Cul Sec in Culemborg won among restaurants, Het Nutshuis in The Hague among MICE venues, and Hotel The Happy Traveler in Groningen took the audience award. The jury sees sustainability in the sector shifting from isolated initiatives to a structural part of the business model.
nieuws.s27t: Van der Valk Hotel Emmen fully renewed after major renovation
nieuws.s27p: After an eighteen-month renovation, all rooms in the original part of Van der Valk Hotel Emmen have been renewed, along with the corridors. Traditional radiators made way for a completely new climate system with air heating and cooling; comfort, functionality and sustainability were central to the design. The hotel grew from 76 to 140 rooms in recent years and is working behind the scenes on a wellness centre expected to open in 2028.
nieuws.s28t: Grid at risk of collapsing this winter at 26 locations, Enexis prepares emergency brake
nieuws.s28p: Grid operator Enexis is taking extra measures at at least 26 locations this winter to prevent overload of the power grid; in the worst case parts of the grid are switched off temporarily. For hotels and hospitality businesses with their own generation, battery storage or charging infrastructure, that underlines yet again the value of an on-site buffer and smart control.
nieuws.s29t: Energy management systems set to work together seamlessly thanks to new ElaadNL framework
nieuws.s29p: ElaadNL has published a framework for interoperable energy management systems, with a concrete choice of five protocols and open-source software; the first interoperability tests are already done. That makes it easier to link EMS, batteries and charging stations from different suppliers to each other.
nieuws.s30t: The Netherlands collects batteries well, but valuable raw materials end up in China
nieuws.s30p: The Netherlands collects discarded batteries properly, but the valuable raw materials disappear to East Asia and especially China. That is the conclusion of Royal Haskoning in a study commissioned by the government. For hoteliers considering battery storage it is a reminder to also look at recycling and residual value when choosing a system.
nieuws.s31t: Council of State: exemption required for solar park in groundwater protection area
nieuws.s31p: The Council of State rules that a solar park in a groundwater protection area is not a facility and requires a provincial exemption as soon as the risk of groundwater contamination increases even slightly. The ruling clarifies the rules for solar installations at sensitive locations.
nieuws.s32t: Up to 6,000 euros subsidy for scrapping your old petrol car and switching to a used electric one
nieuws.s32p: Trading in an old fossil-fuel car for a used electric car can earn up to 6,000 euros in subsidy. The cabinet works with two income brackets – 6,000 euros up to 27,533 euros of aggregate income, 4,000 euros up to 35,793 euros – and a total budget of 52.4 million euros; the final amounts still have to be determined.
nieuws.s33t: Flexible use and briefly doing without power must become ‘the new normal’
nieuws.s33p: State Secretary Jo-Annes de Bat (Climate and Green Growth) wants flexible use of grid connections to become the new normal for citizens and businesses, because the power grid is full. For hotels that means steering more smartly on own generation, battery storage and charging points instead of simply upgrading the connection.
nieuws.s34t: The Netherlands foots the bill for expensive gas storage, cabinet wants to share costs more fairly
nieuws.s34p: The cabinet is considering obliging energy companies to store gas themselves, so that the government has to step in less often when the market fails to fill storage facilities sufficiently. For hotels and hospitality businesses that cook or heat on gas, the gas price therefore remains a cost item to keep in mind.
nieuws.s35t: Tourists spent almost 6 billion euros more than a year earlier
nieuws.s35p: Tourists spent 117.6 billion euros in the Netherlands in 2025, 5.6 billion more than in 2024; foreign guests account for more than half of that growth. Good news for hotels and hospitality businesses, which can absorb higher energy costs more easily as a result.
nieuws.s36t: Cabinet investigates double energy tax on home batteries and bidirectional charging
nieuws.s36p: The cabinet has started a new study into double energy taxation on home batteries and bidirectional charging. Anyone who stores electricity from the grid and feeds it back later sometimes pays energy tax twice on the same kilowatt-hour; research firm Revnext previously calculated that this can save a household 900 to 1,050 euros a year. Results are expected before the end of 2026. For hotels with their own battery or charging square this becomes extra relevant once the net metering scheme ends in 2027.
nieuws.s37t: Flemish households already installed more than 10,000 home batteries this year
nieuws.s37p: Grid operator Fluvius registered more than 10,000 new home batteries in Flanders in the first eight months of 2026; those figures are revised sharply upwards afterwards and the total now stands at around 189,000 installations. The numbers show how fast storage is growing among small consumers. The same is happening in the business market, where batteries dampen peaks for hotels, kitchens and charging squares.
nieuws.s38t: Kloosters service area reopens with fast chargers for electric trucks
nieuws.s38p: Rijkswaterstaat reopened the Kloosters service area on the A58 between Eindhoven and Tilburg after a thorough renovation. Alongside 49 parking spaces it added two fast-charging points for electric freight traffic – still rare along Dutch motorways – and experimented extensively with circular materials and water innovations. An example of how charging infrastructure and climate resilience come together in renovation.
nieuws.s39t: Stricter rules for sustainability claims: ‘green’ has to be substantiated
nieuws.s39p: From 27 September 2026 stricter rules apply to sustainability claims. Terms such as ‘green’ or ‘eco-friendly’ may only be used without further explanation if they meet recognised European or national standards, and own labels without independent verification disappear. The Dutch consumer authority ACM urges companies to review their claims critically. For hotels presenting themselves as sustainable or climate neutral that is a direct reason to take a close look at their communication.
nieuws.s40t: Benefits of sustainable energy use may turn out much bigger
nieuws.s40p: Many scenarios assume an oil price of 64 dollars per barrel and a gas price of 22 cents per cubic metre for 2030, while the market is currently around 100 dollars and above 70 cents. According to the NVDE, the benefit of sustainability is therefore structurally underestimated. CE Delft calculated that solar panels, a heat pump, a battery and an electric car lower energy costs even at a low gas price. Relevant for hotels drawing up an investment plan for after the net metering scheme ends in 2027.
nieuws.s41t: Grid in Brabant can finally breathe thanks to one of the largest batteries in the Netherlands
nieuws.s41p: A battery park with 208 containers is being built in Moerdijk, able to deliver full power for almost three hours, enough to cover the evening peak of around half a million households. Through capacity steering agreements with grid operator TenneT the installation eases congestion in the region, freeing up room for parties on the waiting list. Commissioning is planned for the second quarter of 2028. On a smaller scale, an on-site battery already delivers the same benefit to hotels: fewer peaks, less pressure on the grid.
nieuws.s42t: Open letter: ‘a spot on the grid waiting list should not be for sale’
nieuws.s42p: Grid operators now ask 20 percent of the connection costs upfront just to get on the waiting list, and TenneT 10 percent; depending on the capacity requested that adds up to hundreds of thousands or even millions of euros, without any certainty about the waiting time. A broad coalition of industry and interest groups is calling on the Dutch consumer and market authority ACM to intervene and argues for a maturity test: not the bank balance but the feasibility of a project should decide who comes first. More than 14,000 companies are waiting for transport capacity and nearly 9,000 generators are stuck in long queues. For hotels that need a heavier connection, the down payment has become a real hurdle.
nieuws.s43t: Real acceleration of battery storage arrives in 2027: ‘then you see on your energy bill how much it saves’
nieuws.s43p: With the net metering scheme ending on 1 January 2027, growth in battery storage is only really starting, market experts expect. A household currently uses about 30 percent of its own solar power directly; with a battery that rises to 65 to 70 percent, and in some regions owners will soon be paid when the grid operator uses the battery to fight grid congestion. Dutch households had 167,000 battery systems installed in 2025, sales double again this year and half a million systems are expected in 2027. The same calculation applies to hotels: use your own generation first, and only then the grid.
nieuws.hn8t: Savills: EPBD IV creates a major sustainability task for retail and hotels
nieuws.hn8p: More than half of the total floor area of retail and hotel space in the Netherlands does not meet the tightened European energy performance requirements (EPBD IV), or has no energy label at all. That is the conclusion of an analysis by Savills. For hoteliers it means that a label and a concrete sustainability plan increasingly determine the financeability and lettability of the property.
nieuws.hn9t: Five hotels in Drenthe work on circular hotel rooms
nieuws.hn9p: Five hotels in Drenthe are developing a circular hotel room design together with students and architects. The Circular Hotel Rooms Drenthe project started on 24 September and gives hoteliers a concrete starting point for sustainability: smarter use of materials, maintenance and lifespan should save costs in the longer term. Participants are City hotel de Jonge, Hotel Eeserhof, Landhuishotel Rikus, Landhotel Diever and Hotel Wesseling; the knowledge is collected in an online knowledge base for other entrepreneurs.
nieuws.s44t: EV sales accelerate: almost 90,000 electric cars added in eight months
nieuws.s44p: In the first eight months of 2026 almost 90,000 fully electric cars were registered in the Netherlands. Their share of new car sales rose to 39.3 percent, against 34.4 percent a year earlier, and more than 750,000 EVs are now on the road, 8.1 percent of the total fleet. According to the Trend Report published by RVO, electric cars are also becoming structurally more attractive: in four years the price gap with petrol in the compact classes narrowed from 9,000 to 3,000-5,000 euros, range keeps rising and fast charging is getting faster. For hotels it simply means more charging demand in their own car park.
nieuws.s45t: ‘Also interesting for businesses’: new guide on batteries and the end of net metering
nieuws.s45p: In ‘De Thuisbatterij Gids’ author Keesjan Deelstra explains how battery storage, an energy management system and a dynamic contract work together once the net metering scheme ends. According to him the principle is identical for a home and for a hundred batteries in a sea container: battery chemistry, inverters, capacity and efficiency work the same way, only the rules for commercial C&I projects differ, as do the requirements for cold and heat. One detail that matters for businesses: with a so-called converter connection you pay no energy tax on purchases, while private owners lose roughly 11 cents per kilowatt-hour of tax after 2026 and therefore need a larger spread.
nieuws.s46t: Energy bill rises 140 euros a year due to jump in grid tariffs
nieuws.s46p: Dutch regulator ACM expects grid tariffs to rise by an average of 19 percent next year: about 89 euros more for electricity and 52 euros for gas for an average household, roughly 12 euros per month. Companies connected to TenneT’s high-voltage grid also face a considerably higher bill. The money goes mainly into expanding the power grid. For hotels the fixed part of the energy bill therefore rises regardless of consumption, which makes own generation and battery storage more attractive.
nieuws.s47t: New monthly record for home batteries: 8,535 new units, 1 gigawatt threshold passed
nieuws.s47p: Grid operators registered 8,535 new batteries in September, the strongest month so far. Cumulative capacity behind the meter passes 1 gigawatt for the first time; among large consumers 72 systems with an inverter capacity of up to 1 megawatt were added. Storage is rapidly becoming a fixed part of the energy system, and for hotels the business case for their own battery is becoming increasingly normal.
nieuws.s48t: Utrecht and grid operators launch Megaflex: new connections possible again from 2028
nieuws.s48p: The Utrecht region has been completely closed to new electricity connections for three months. With the Megaflex plan the province and the grid operators want to free up room through smart and flexible use of the existing grid, so that new connections are possible again from 2028. Businesses are encouraged to flatten peaks and store power themselves; the waiting list is worked through step by step and the pace differs per area.
nieuws.s49t: Grid congestion spreads to Noord-Brabant and Noord-Holland, state secretary De Bat defends approach in parliament
nieuws.s49p: After Flevoland, Gelderland and Utrecht, Noord-Brabant now also threatens to close to new power connections, with Noord-Holland following. State secretary De Bat confirmed in parliament that a connection freeze for small consumers applies in Utrecht-Noord until 1 January 2027 and that the cabinet is extending its crisis approach to the areas of greatest need. Grid operators put the cost of expanding the grid until 2040 at 270 billion euros; consultancy BCG estimates the annual economic damage from grid congestion at 10 to 40 billion euros.
nieuws.s50t: Batteries as a waiting-list ticket: Zuid-Holland launches action plan for scarce grid capacity
nieuws.s50p: Almost all of Zuid-Holland faces grid congestion, spread across six areas. The Zuid-Holland Energy Council presents an action plan to use scarce grid capacity better, with batteries as a route to a connection sooner. The approach fits the broader line in the province: do not wait for grid expansion, but distribute the space that exists more cleverly.
nieuws.s51t: Cheapest energy offer more than 800 euros pricier, yet nearly half do not compare contracts
nieuws.s51p: The cheapest one-year energy contract has become more than 800 euros more expensive in nine months. Yet nearly half of the Dutch do not compare their energy contract, which this year already costs them roughly that amount. It underlines how important it remains to compare tariffs and contract types closely, also for businesses with a large-consumer connection.
nieuws.s52t: Flevoland home battery subsidy pot empty: no more applications this year
nieuws.s52p: The home battery subsidy pot of the province of Flevoland is exhausted for 2026. The maximum number of applications for the round that opened on 1 October has been reached and new applications are no longer accepted. It is a sign that demand for storage support exceeds the available budget, while interest in batteries keeps growing.
nieuws.s53t: 60 percent of power renewable in third quarter, growth mainly from biomass
nieuws.s53p: In the third quarter 60 percent of electricity for domestic consumption came from renewable sources, two percentage points more than a year earlier. The growth came entirely from biomass, through more co-firing in coal plants; solar and wind delivered less because capacity expansion is stagnating. Because there were fewer surpluses, less green power was curtailed temporarily.
nieuws.s55t: Winter will determine the gas price and how tight supplies are
nieuws.s56t: Energy for entrepreneurs 2026: contracts, deductions and subsidies
nieuws.s57t: Solar market recovers slightly, commercial roofs lead the growth
nieuws.s57p: Grid operators registered 8,724 new solar installations in September, almost 12 percent more than in August. The recovery comes mainly from the commercial segment: systems larger than 15 kilowatts grew fastest and large consumers are the only category performing better than a year earlier. Total registered inverter capacity is approaching 20 gigawatts. Larger rooftop systems are becoming the norm, which further strengthens the business case for own generation combined with storage.
nieuws.s58t: New RVO subsidy for energy hubs: 9.6 million euros for research on business parks
nieuws.s58p: From 1 October businesses can apply to RVO for the new Energy Hubs Research subsidy (EHUB). In an energy hub, companies align local generation, storage, use and transport, so they make better use of the electricity grid. 9.6 million euros is available for an exploratory scan or a more extensive study; the government aims for five hundred active energy hubs by 2030.
nieuws.s59t: Belgium tightens rules against double subsidies for batteries
nieuws.s59p: The Belgian Council of Ministers approved a draft royal decree that explicitly applies the ban on subsidy cumulation in the capacity remuneration mechanism (CRM) to energy storage. A battery operator that already receives other support may not simultaneously claim CRM payments. Supervision powers become clearer and data exchange between the regions and the federal government is arranged.
nieuws.s60t: Court: solar panel yield may not be kept outside the service costs
nieuws.s60p: The District Court of Zeeland-West-Brabant upheld a ruling by the Rent Tribunal: a landlord who kept the yield of solar panels outside the service cost statement may not pass on the full electricity costs. Only service costs actually incurred are chargeable. The court also held it against the landlord that he had not applied for an available government compensation scheme.
nieuws.s61t: Germany opens the door to bidirectional charging: car battery may serve as home battery
nieuws.s61p: The German regulator Bundesnetzagentur adopted the MiSpeL rules. In Germany, owners of subsidised solar panels may from now on use their electric car's battery flexibly without losing the EEG subsidy; charging points are officially treated as stationary batteries. A demarcation option or a flat-rate option up to 30 kilowatts peak determines which share of the stored power qualifies for subsidy.
nieuws.s62t: GIGA Storage: 350-megawatt Albatross battery project ready to build in Germany
nieuws.s62p: The Dutch company GIGA Storage reached 'Ready to Build' status for its Albatross energy storage project (350 MW / 1,400 MWh) near Neuenkirchen in Lower Saxony, directly next to the 380kV Merzen substation. With 264 battery units the project can cover the daily consumption of around 193,000 households. Construction starts in the first half of 2027, commissioning follows in 2028.
nieuws.s63t: Enkhuizen allows solar panels on historic facades
nieuws.s63p: The municipality of Enkhuizen relaxed its aesthetics policy for the protected townscape: visible solar panels are no longer refused as a rule but assessed case by case, with the historic character as the starting point. In the city centre a permit with a placement plan remains mandatory; anyone who already has panels without a permit must apply for one before 1 January 2027.
nieuws.s64t: Feed-in waiting list shrinks slightly, requested capacity rises 13 percent
nieuws.s64p: At the end of June the regional grid operators had 8,558 feed-in requests on the waiting list, slightly fewer than the 8,612 at the end of last year. The requested transport capacity did rise in six months from 5,027 to 5,693 megawatts, more than 13 percent. The waiting list for consumption grew to 15,498 requests. For hotels with their own generation the conclusion remains that using and storing power yourself pays off better than feeding it back.
nieuws.s65t: Waiting list for the power grid grows again, but grid operators also see hopeful signs
nieuws.s65p: Almost 15,500 companies and organisations are waiting for a heavier power connection, over 300 more than six months ago. Growth is flattening and in a few regions the waiting list is even falling. Utrecht remains the problem area, where the regions around Amersfoort and Food Valley are closing to new connections. More and more companies therefore choose a flexible contract without a full-time right to power, in exchange for a discount.
nieuws.s66t: MOOI subsidy scheme prioritises flexible perovskite solar panels and energy hubs
nieuws.s66p: The MOOI subsidy scheme opens this year under three themes: Electricity, Built Environment and Industry. Minister Van Veldhoven prioritises flexible perovskite solar panels, circularity and energy hubs in which businesses align their energy use with each other. Those hubs should also reduce grid congestion. The technology is already available, the minister says; the bottlenecks now lie in execution: space, people, raw materials and cooperation.
nieuws.s67t: Consumers pay more for other products too because of high energy prices
nieuws.s67p: High energy prices caused by the conflict in the Middle East pushed inflation to 3.4 percent in the Netherlands and 3.8 percent in the eurozone in September. According to ING chief economist Bert Colijn, businesses pass their higher energy costs on to consumers, and the fear is that this spills over into categories such as food. For hotels it means the energy bill remains a cost item that demands steering.
nieuws.s68t: Impact of the full power grid becomes increasingly clear for ’s-Hertogenbosch
nieuws.s68p: New figures from grid operator Enexis show that for around 2,600 of the more than 4,200 registered homes in ’s-Hertogenbosch no grid capacity is available for the time being; those projects are on the waiting list. Grid congestion affects not only housing construction, but also businesses, mobility and the energy transition. Together with entrepreneurs, the municipality focuses on grid-conscious building, smart charging and energy hubs.
nieuws.hn10t: 15,500 businesses are waiting for extra power: how entrepreneurs find space themselves
nieuws.hn10p: The waiting list for the power grid holds almost 15,500 businesses and organisations. While grid operators cannot scale up substantially before 2030, entrepreneurs are creating space themselves: by lowering peaks, generating and storing their own energy, or sharing power in an energy hub. For hotels with growth plans, flexibility in energy use often helps sooner than waiting for a larger connection.
nieuws.hn11t: No room on the power grid? This company runs on its own energy 365 days a year: 'We do everything ourselves'
nieuws.hn11p: A company that could not get space on the power grid built its own energy system and now runs on self-generated power all year round. The example shows how entrepreneurs can work around grid congestion by combining generation, storage and smart control. That is relevant for hotels, where charging points, cooling and kitchen equipment create large peaks together.
nieuws.hn12t: Energy hub De President live: businesses share grid capacity together
nieuws.hn12p: At the De President business park in Hoofddorp, companies have been sharing their available grid and flexibility capacity through a single energy hub since 4 June, so that together they get more out of the same grid. The festive go-live took place on 8 October, at Hotel De President. That hotel is connected to the hub with its own smart energy system and shows what an energy hub delivers for a site with a full connection.
nieuws.hn13t: Relais & Châteaux takes next step in sustainable gastronomy
nieuws.hn13p: Twenty chefs from Relais & Châteaux gathered in Lisbon for the World Culinary Council. The association reports that 90 percent of its 580 member hotels and restaurants no longer serve eel, and it is urging European ministers to introduce a temporary ban on eel fishing. Sustainability thus remains a visible part of the hospitality offering; for hotels with a restaurant, the menu is one of the most visible places to show it.
nieuws.s69t: Grid tariffs from 2029 higher at peak hours, lower off-peak
nieuws.s69p: The Dutch consumer authority ACM wants to reform electricity transport tariffs: from 2029 users pay more at busy moments and less during off-peak hours. About a third of the tariff remains a fixed amount, the rest depends on how much power you use and when. For businesses with a battery or smart control, shifting consumption to quiet hours becomes more rewarding.
nieuws.s70t: €200 extra subsidy for smart heat pumps, subsidy for triple glazing halved
nieuws.s70p: The cabinet is adjusting the ISDE subsidy from 1 January 2027. Smart, controllable heat pumps that communicate via an open protocol such as EEBus, S2 or Matter receive a €200 bonus, while the subsidy per kilowatt of thermal capacity drops from €225 to €120. The subsidy for triple glazing with new frames falls from €111 to €55 per square metre. Steering to quiet moments should thus relieve the power grid.
nieuws.s71t: Electrifying without waiting for grid expansion
nieuws.s71p: Installation company Batenburg opened the Smart Solar Energy Hub in Twello: battery storage, energy management, charging infrastructure and on-site generation in one installation, within the existing grid connection. Smart control shifts consumption to moments when the grid has room, so businesses can electrify or expand without waiting for a heavier connection.
nieuws.s72t: National Charging Survey 2026: EV drivers charge ever smarter
nieuws.s72p: Of the EV drivers who charge at home, 90 percent now apply smart charging: charging at cheap moments, using their own solar power or avoiding peaks on the grid. Nearly half have a dynamic energy contract and more than a quarter have a home battery. Bidirectional charging is gaining ground: 24 percent want to apply it within a year. For hotels with charge points in the car park, the survey shows where guest expectations are heading.
nieuws.s73t: On-site solar and battery make new build possible despite grid congestion
nieuws.s73p: Construction has started on business park Vosdonk Zuid in Etten-Leur for two units combining offices and a warehouse. The building will have around 1,260 solar panels, battery storage, a smart energy management system and twenty charging points, allowing it to run on a small grid connection. The approach is interesting for hotels too: generate and store on site first, and only then request grid capacity.
nieuws.s74t: Green gas blending obligation one step closer, extra costs up to 1.5 cents per cubic metre
nieuws.s74p: The implementing regulation for the green gas blending obligation has been sent to the Council of State. From 2027 gas suppliers must include a growing share of green gas in their supplies, rising to an annual CO2 reduction of 2.85 megaton from 2031. In the first year the extra costs stay limited to a maximum of 1.5 cents per cubic metre, but they rise to a maximum of 9 cents towards 2031. For hotels with a gas-fired kitchen or boiler that means a gradually rising gas bill, which makes electrification profitable sooner.
nieuws.s75t: Limited grid connection, fast charging thanks to batteries
nieuws.s75p: Carwash A27 in Nieuwegein could not get a larger connection, so it solved it itself: 274 kWp of solar panels, 964 kWh of batteries and DC fast chargers behind the existing grid connection. Smart control decides when cars charge and when the battery steps in. For hotels with a busy car park and a tight connection it is the same route: generate and store on site first, then charge.
nieuws.s76t: 'Charging points need more attention and love'
nieuws.s76p: DC charging plazas are mostly about fast roll-out and too little about maintenance and electrical safety. A DC specialist therefore calls for a mandatory inspection regime with fixed checks and professionals who keep the overall picture. For hotels with fast chargers on site that is a useful warning: a charging point is an installation that needs periodic maintenance, just like a lift or a refrigeration system.
nieuws.s77t: Meter cupboard safety: 'It is not a question of if it goes wrong, but when'
nieuws.s77p: Electrical accidents in the meter cupboard drew a lot of attention this summer, and the mistakes from the solar panel market now seem to be repeating themselves with batteries: an extra circuit group and done. A troubleshooter sees too little attention for the existing cupboard, heat management and cable diameter. His advice is simple: start with an inspection and a fixed step-by-step plan. Relevant for any hotel where solar panels, charging points and storage come together in the same meter cupboard.
nieuws.s78t: Flex-e: apply until 15 October for a scan, study or flexibility measures
nieuws.s78p: Large-scale consumers can apply to RVO for a subsidy for flexible electricity consumption until 15 October. The scheme has three parts: a flexibility scan, a feasibility study and the implementation of flexibility measures such as battery storage and smart control. For hotels with a connection larger than 3x80 amps that want to grow or become more sustainable within their existing connection, this is the most direct subsidy route.
nieuws.s79t: Grid operators want mandatory registration of charging points and heat pumps
nieuws.s79p: In a new system analysis on grid congestion, Netbeheer Nederland repeats its call to make registration of charging points and heat pumps mandatory. Those devices are barely mapped today, while they do load the low-voltage grid. For hotels with charging points and a heat pump it pays to have the installation data complete now, so that a future registration duty holds no surprises.
nieuws.s80t: Tenth group transport agreement: three companies in Lelystad share grid capacity
nieuws.s80p: Three companies on the Noordersluis business park in Lelystad signed a group transport agreement and now share a single transport contract. It is the tenth such agreement for grid operator Liander, and the formula is gaining ground on business parks as a way to find space on a full power grid. For hotels on a park with other businesses it is a route to more capacity together, without waiting for a heavier connection.
nieuws.s81t: CBS: number of large-scale batteries in the Netherlands more than tripled
nieuws.s81p: The Netherlands counted 286 large batteries of 1 megawatt hour or more at the end of 2025, against 84 a year earlier. Together they account for 753 megawatts of power and 1,575 megawatt hours of storage capacity, according to new CBS figures, with the strongest growth in systems between 1 and 10 megawatt hours. Battery storage is now a mature part of the energy system, also for businesses that want to flatten their peak demand.
nieuws.hn14t: Hotel construction 2026: plenty of plans, but the road to opening gets longer
nieuws.hn14p: The first four editions of Hotelbouwplannen 2026 list 59 new plans, 35 permit procedures and 88 updates on previously reported projects. Lead times of eight to twelve years are no longer exceptional, and besides procedures and objections, grid congestion adds further delay. For hotels with construction or sustainability plans it means: bring the energy infrastructure into the planning as early as possible.
nieuws.hn15t: KHN asks cabinet for a task force against regulatory pressure in hospitality
nieuws.hn15p: KHN wants the cabinet to set up a task force that makes sure the promise to scrap 500 rules a year actually becomes noticeable for entrepreneurs. The sector works on razor-thin margins because of higher costs for energy, purchasing and staff, and fears extra charges such as a higher water tax. Besides less regulation, KHN asks for a firm ceiling on tourist tax.
nieuws.s82t: Energy saving obligation tightened to 7 years, deferral possible when the grid is full
nieuws.s82p: The energy saving obligation changes on 1 July 2027: the required payback period rises from 5 to 7 years, so businesses using at least 50,000 kilowatt hours of electricity or 25,000 cubic metres of gas must implement a broader set of measures. New is that entrepreneurs who cannot get a larger connection because of grid congestion may temporarily postpone electrification measures; a statement from the grid operator is enough as proof. For hotels this means a longer list of mandatory measures, while deferral is justified as long as the grid cannot deliver the expansion.
nieuws.s83t: Flex market for grid congestion now public: bid on every request
nieuws.s83p: Grid operators now publish their need for flexible capacity on one public platform, so providers of flexibility can see at a glance where and when the power grid needs support. At launch a request for 496 megawatts is open, with contracts running from day-ahead to multi-year. More flexible capacity in the right place shortens the waiting list of more than 15,500 businesses waiting for a connection, and makes it more interesting for hotels with a battery or smart control to bid in.
nieuws.s84t: Two-way contracts act in parliament: concerns about incentives for storage
nieuws.s84p: The House of Representatives is reviewing the act that introduces two-way contracts as the successor to the SDE++ scheme for new wind and solar projects. Under such a contract for difference the government tops up the difference when the market price falls below an agreed reference price, and the producer pays back when prices are high. Parliament wants guarantees that enough incentives remain for energy storage and flexibility, because a contract per kilowatt hour does not steer on when power is delivered.
nieuws.s85t: More than half of EV drivers want bidirectional charging at home
