nieuws.s85p: More than half of electric drivers want to charge bidirectionally at home, using the car as a buffer for their house or the grid. Of the 2,399 respondents, 24 percent want that arranged within a year and 45 percent name reducing grid congestion as a motive. The main brake is the battery warranty and worries about wear. For hotels with charging points on site this signals that guests and staff will increasingly bring a car that can feed power back.
nieuws.s86t: Energie Samen: at least 50 percent local ownership for battery parks
nieuws.s86p: Energie Samen is asking the cabinet to let energy communities own at least 50 percent of storage projects from the start. According to the umbrella organisation it matters who owns and steers the battery: storage that mainly pays off for a market party contributes less to a stable grid than a battery that supports the local supply. The organisation also wants subsidies to focus on collective storage in areas with grid congestion instead of on all storage.
nieuws.s87t: Solar panels saved 2.7 billion euros in fossil imports this year
nieuws.s87p: Renewable energy and electric driving saved the Netherlands 7.7 billion euros in imported fossil energy between 1 March and 1 October, of which 2.7 billion came from solar power. The country still depends on imports for 77 percent of its energy use, a share that PBL expects to fall to 67 percent by 2030. The outcome underlines that generating and storing your own power is a direct buffer against swings in gas and oil prices.
nieuws.s88t: Grid operators: outage risk doubles to 800,000 households
nieuws.s88p: Netbeheer Nederland warns that the number of households on a low-voltage grid with an increased risk of outages doubles from around 400,000 now to roughly 800,000 in 2035. Solar panels are the main cause of bottlenecks in those grids until 2030, not charging points or heat pumps. Where outages occur inverters drop out and heat pumps or charging points stop working; on-site storage and smart control prevent such a moment from hitting operations directly.
nieuws.s89t: First standard for smart heat pumps published, battery standard to follow
nieuws.s89p: NEN has published NTA 8171, the agreement describing how smart heat pumps communicate with the power grid and with other appliances so that grid capacity is used better. The standard covers installations up to 70 kilowatts thermal on the low-voltage grid, in homes and businesses alike. Similar agreements for charging points, home batteries, inverters and energy management systems are in the making and should be finished this year or by the first quarter of 2027. Smart control is thus step by step becoming a condition, including for subsidies.
nieuws.s90t: Cabinet sticks to mandatory hybrid heat pump from 2029
nieuws.s90p: The cabinet is holding on to the mandatory hybrid heat pump when a gas boiler is replaced from 2029, despite criticism from the PVV and questions from the VVD about affordability. A hybrid heat pump of 4 kilowatts costs 6,200 euros on average, of which 2,125 euros comes back through the ISDE subsidy. The exact standard will only follow in spring 2027. Hotels with an ageing boiler installation are wise to include their heat supply in multi-year planning now.
nieuws.s91t: 90 percent of home chargers charge smart, nearly half have a dynamic contract
nieuws.s91p: The National Charging Survey 2026 by RVO, ElaadNL and the Electric Drivers Association shows that 90 percent of home chargers now charge smart and that nearly half have a dynamic power contract, against 13 percent three years ago. Two thirds charge when their own solar panels produce power and 45 percent avoid the evening peak between 16:00 and 21:00. For hotels with charging points it means that guests and staff expect charging to happen at the cheapest and quietest moment.
nieuws.s92t: Stedin can connect 90 percent of registered housing, 24,400 homes wait
nieuws.s92p: Stedin has enough grid capacity for 90 percent of the registered housing projects: of more than 270,000 registered homes, around 253,000 can be connected. The remaining 24,400 homes are on the waiting list at roughly 18 full electricity stations. Grid operator, municipalities and developers are moving towards grid-aware construction, and since 1 October municipalities can request grid capacity ten years ahead through the Earlier Application procedure. For hotels with building plans it means: reserve capacity early and put the energy design at the front of the plan.
nieuws.hn16t: On sustainability you do not compete
nieuws.hn16p: Sustainability mainly delivers cost savings for hotels rather than extra revenue: the ratio is roughly 80 percent efficiency gains against 20 percent additional turnover, says Philip Steiner, chief operating officer of hotel operator and investor Vertiq Hospitality Partners, in an interview with Hospitality Management. Investors increasingly look at the financing benefit: given two comparable hotels, the greener property gets cheaper financing because it carries less risk tomorrow. His advice to the sector is to share best practices, because on sustainability alone you no longer compete.
nieuws.hn17t: Stayokay Rotterdam made sustainable: insulation and a new installation concept in the Cube Houses
nieuws.hn17p: The large-scale renovation of Stayokay Rotterdam in the Cube Houses has been completed. The facades are insulated from the inside, the roofs were insulated and the entire installation concept was renewed with air handling and energy-efficient systems that can cool and heat. Existing bunk beds were given a second life and renewable bamboo was used for new interior elements. The project shows that sustainability is possible even in a listed building with little installation space.
nieuws.s93t: Cabinet promises a solution for double energy tax on home batteries
nieuws.s93p: The double energy tax on home batteries and bidirectional charging has been included in the 500-rules programme, the package with which the cabinet wants to scrap regulations. The ministries of Finance and Economic Affairs are working with the sector on a solution that takes effect after 2026. Anyone who stores power from the grid and feeds it back later sometimes pays energy tax twice on the same kilowatt hour. For hotels with their own battery or charging square this offers concrete prospects of an end to that double charge.
nieuws.s94t: RDI warns: cyberattack on inverters and home batteries can hit the power grid
nieuws.s94p: A targeted cyberattack or a faulty software update can disable solar inverters, home batteries, charging points and heat pumps at the same time and destabilise the power grid. That is the warning from the Dutch Digital Infrastructure Inspectorate (RDI). Because those devices are controlled remotely, the vulnerability sits in the software and in the chain behind it. For hotels with their own generation, storage and charging points it underlines the importance of secure updates and of an installation that keeps working when remote control drops out.
nieuws.s95t: Grid operators expect a flexibility shortfall of 6.4 gigawatts in 2030
nieuws.s95p: In the most conservative scenario of the first Dutch Flexibility Needs Assessment a shortfall of flexible capacity of up to 6.4 gigawatts looms in 2030, concentrated in the evening and the morning. Those are exactly the moments when a hotel switches on kitchen, lighting and charging points at the same time. The analysis shows how much room can be gained with smart steering and storage, before the grid is reinforced.
nieuws.s96t: Solar power accounts for 67 percent of system curtailment in 2030
nieuws.s96p: In the first Dutch Flexibility Needs Assessment solar panels are responsible for 67 percent of all curtailment at system level in 2030, because output is increasingly capped on sunny afternoons. Total curtailment falls again towards 2035, as storage and flexibility absorb the surpluses. For hotels with a large roof area this means that using and storing power yourself matters more than feeding back at the moment everyone else does.
nieuws.s97t: SDE++ 2025: Gelderland gets the most solar subsidy, Brabant the most projects
nieuws.s97p: The 2025 SDE++ round awarded the province of Gelderland the most subsidy for solar panels: over 87 million euros. Noord-Brabant received the highest number of grants of all twelve provinces. The analysis shows where a lot of solar power will be added in the coming years, which helps hotels judge how full the grid in their region will become and whether their own generation with storage beats feeding back.
nieuws.hn18t: National hotel growth hides losses in the border provinces
nieuws.hn18p: Dutch hotels recorded 2.4 percent more overnight stays in July and August 2026 than a year earlier, but in the seven border provinces the number fell by 4.5 percent. Noord- and Zuid-Holland gained 282,000 Dutch hotel nights this summer, while the border provinces lost 181,000. Over the twelve months to the end of August 2026 the border provinces shed 984,000 overnight stays, a drop of 5.1 percent, while Noord- and Zuid-Holland grew by 2.6 percent. Hotel revenue excluding VAT fell 2.0 percent nationally in the second quarter, more than the number of overnight stays. For hotels this means a national average says little; your own region and source markets give the real picture.
nieuws.hn19t: CityHub opens a hotel in Berlin in existing retail space
nieuws.hn19p: CityHub announces a hotel at Leipziger Platz in Berlin, with 139 Hubs, 17 of which are suitable for guests with a disability. The chain is not building new, but converting around 2,100 square metres of existing retail space in a mixed-use building. Reuse instead of new construction and a modular plug-and-play design should cut the project's CO2 emissions considerably. For hotels working on renovation or expansion themselves, it shows that reusing existing space is a route to less energy and less material.
nieuws.hn20t: Travel Trends 2027: guests pay more attention to health and budget
nieuws.hn20p: The annual Travel Trends survey among more than 28,000 travellers, including 1,006 Dutch respondents, shows that health and lifestyle weigh more heavily in travel choices: 54 percent say a change in health or lifestyle influenced them, and 68 percent consider at least one healthy, balanced meal option in the hotel important. Budget differences play a role too: 40 percent have doubted at some point with whom to travel because of differing budgets. For hotels this means more demand for clear pricing, flexible options and food and drink that fits different lifestyles.
nieuws.s98t: Without net metering, a building reaches 80 to 90 percent self-consumption with storage
nieuws.s98p: With net metering ending in 2027, self-consumption becomes the entire business case for solar panels. Anyone who changes nothing loses about two thirds of the benefit; adding a heat pump, a battery or a solar boiler lifts self-consumption to 80 to 90 percent. A 5 kilowatt-hour home battery adds about 38 percent self-consumption, and a solar boiler captures roughly 44 percent of annual output. Behaviour alone, such as running the dishwasher on sunny hours, adds only 6 percent. For hotels the same arithmetic applies at a larger scale: the more consumption coincides with own generation, the less power goes back to the grid at feed-in rates.
nieuws.s99t: Parliament wants energy tax on net consumption for bidirectional charging
nieuws.s99p: The Dutch parliament adopted a D66 motion asking the cabinet to study whether energy tax for bidirectional shared cars at fixed locations can be levied on net consumption only. Such cars can act as a rolling neighbourhood battery, taking power from the grid and feeding it back, which eases grid congestion. The motion is limited to connections without their own solar panels, because the calculation is technically simplest there, and asks for lost tax revenue to be weighed against avoided grid investments. Only the PVV, FVD and Groep Markuszower voted against. For hotels with a charging yard this is the same principle that already applies to batteries: power you store and feed back later should not be taxed twice.
nieuws.s100t: SDE++ 2025: 88 business roofs subsidised, logistics real estate dominates
nieuws.s100p: The 2025 SDE++ round awarded subsidy to 88 solar roofs on business premises. Building chain Hornbach received more than 2.3 million euros across four decisions, chipmaker ASML 3.5 million euros for its Oirschot site and Quooker over 600,000 euros for Ridderkerk. Logistics real estate dominates again: one Belgian property investor received 16.9 million euros for six projects. Supermarket chains are absent this time, and municipalities and water authorities barely feature. Since the Council of State ruled on the openness of RVO data, awarded capacities per project are no longer visible, so this analysis is not a complete picture.
nieuws.s101t: Nijmegen manufacturer stores solar power and earns from the energy market
nieuws.s101p: A Nijmegen manufacturer of precision parts has commissioned three battery containers, together 375 kilowatts of power and 783 kilowatt-hours of storage. Its solar panels generate more than the machines consume; the surplus no longer flows back to the grid but is stored, used on site and traded on the energy market through a dynamic contract. Because the battery absorbs peaks, the company can use more power without upgrading its main connection, which on a congested grid often means months of waiting. An emergency power supply will be added later this year. Exactly the combination that suits hotels with a kitchen, laundry and charging points: own generation first, the grid second.
nieuws.hn21t: Hotels around Zaanstad: mixed occupancy and tourist tax as a concern
nieuws.hn21p: The periodic hotel meeting of KHN Zaanstreek showed mixed occupancy: some hotels perform well, others lag behind, and the balance between business and leisure guests is shifting. Guests come from a wide range of countries, from the United Kingdom to China, India, Italy and Spain. Besides rising operating costs, tourist tax is the main worry: for 2027 an inflation correction of about 2 percent is on the table, after which the municipality will also look at river cruises and day visitors. The pipeline includes a 144-room hotel in the old silos in Wormerveer and a hostel with more than 328 beds. With more supply and higher costs per room, using energy more efficiently is one of the few line items a hotel can lower structurally.
nieuws.hn22t: Water tax ceiling disappears: hotels and wellness pay more
nieuws.hn22p: The ceiling on the Dutch tax on tap water is being phased out. In 2025 companies paid tax only on the first 300 cubic metres, in 2026 the threshold is 50,000 cubic metres and from 2027 the ceiling disappears entirely. Water-intensive businesses such as hotels, saunas and wellness centres face a substantial increase in costs, KHN warns. Together with VNO-NCW, MKB-Nederland, HISWA-RECRON and Gastvrij Nederland the trade body spent years raising the consequences and doubts whether a higher price actually leads to lower use: in hospitality, water is mainly needed for cleaning, sanitary facilities, rooms and kitchens. Now that the measure is fact, KHN focuses on a workable implementation and on measures that demonstrably save water.
nieuws.s102t: Emergency power in Houten: batteries and generators must cover the winter peak
nieuws.s102p: Grid operator Stedin is placing temporary diesel generators and containers full of batteries on a site in the east of Houten. The facility only kicks in when the power grid threatens to become overloaded: the batteries deliver first, then the generators, which run on renewable fuel. The installation arrives at the Schonauwenseweg next month and is removed again in April 2027; Stedin and TenneT expect the emergency power will be needed for at most 58 hours this winter. Because the permit has not yet been granted, the municipality is examining whether the containers can be tolerated temporarily. For hotels with expansion plans in the province of Utrecht this means grid capacity will become tighter rather than looser for the time being.
nieuws.s103t: Grid waiting list grows to almost 15,500, though growth is levelling off
nieuws.s103p: The number of companies and organisations waiting for a connection or for more power rose by over 300 in the first half of 2026 to almost 15,500, according to figures from Netbeheer Nederland. In the province of Utrecht the regions around Amersfoort and Food Valley are now also closed; priority connections there must wait until 2028. More and more companies are choosing a flexible contract, taking less power at peak moments in exchange for a discount. In the first half of 2026 as many companies faced such restrictions as in the whole of 2025. For hotels with a fully used connection or expansion plans that is the most realistic route for now: request capacity with a consumption pattern that fits the grid.
nieuws.s104t: ISDE applications hit a yearly peak in September: 39.8 million euros
nieuws.s104p: Households applied for 39.8 million euros in ISDE subsidy in September, the highest monthly amount of 2026, with 20,005 applications covering 29,038 devices. Insulation passed the 24 million euro mark for the first time this year at 24.8 million, while heat pumps rose from 11 to 14.8 million euros. From January through September the total stands at 306.8 million euros, 3 percent more than last year, as insulation grew 20 percent and heat pumps fell 19 percent. In the business market heat pump applications recovered from 1.2 to 2.1 million euros, still half below the July peak. For hotels with ageing installations business ISDE therefore remains the first point of contact, although business applications continue to lag household ones.
nieuws.s105t: Postcode-roos subsidy stays unused: 84 percent of the budget is left on the table
nieuws.s105p: Energy cooperatives and homeowners' associations applied for 12.4 million euros this year under the Dutch subsidy scheme for cooperative energy generation (SCE), out of 78 million euros available. That leaves 84 percent of the budget unused, a pattern that repeats itself: in 2025 most of the 100 million euros also stayed on the table. Costs for security, insurance and financing rose while green power prices fell, and the PBL does not count a return on member investments through profit rights. For hotels with a large roof a cooperative solar roof remains technically interesting, but the business case depends on a scheme that first needs a thorough overhaul.
nieuws.s106t: Brabant takes charge of new high-voltage substation in Central Brabant
nieuws.s106p: North Brabant has started a project procedure for a combined 150/20-kilovolt substation with underground cables in the Hilvarenbeek, Oirschot and Oisterwijk region. Transmission operator TenneT is the initiator and works with regional grid operator Enexis; the province becomes the competent authority itself to speed up procedures. The formal start document is expected in November, the location is not yet fixed and residents, businesses and landowners are involved in the elaboration. For hotels in the region it mainly brings long-term clarity: a new connection or expansion will still take months.
nieuws.s107t: Four Dutch recycling projects receive strategic status from the EU
nieuws.s107p: The European Union has designated four Dutch projects as strategic under the Critical Raw Materials Act, including battery recycler Back2Battery, which recovers lithium, cobalt, nickel, manganese and graphite through hydrometallurgy and targets 26,000 tonnes a year, around 10 percent of the European market in 2030. CRITICAL. eventually recovers 24 elements from discarded printed circuit boards and plans a plant in Frankenberg that processes 80 tonnes of old solar panels a day, a million panels a year. That plant should open in the first quarter of 2028. For hotels with solar panels or a battery the end-of-life chain becomes shorter and less dependent on imports.
nieuws.s108t: Home battery saves heat pump owners up to 230 euros in grid costs by 2030
nieuws.s108p: CE Delft modelled eight housing types for the Dutch homeowners' association under the new grid tariff of regulator ACM, in which two thirds of transport costs depend on when and how much power you draw. An all-electric heat pump comes to 940 euros in annual grid costs, against 850 euros for a hybrid heat pump and 660 euros for a home with a gas boiler. A home battery cuts that amount by 230 euros in 2030, because it charges outside the expensive time blocks. For hotels with charging points and a battery the same logic applies: charging and consuming at the right moments becomes a direct saving on grid costs.
nieuws.hn23t: Opening a restaurant is quick in the Netherlands, the energy bill then decides the margin
nieuws.hn23p: The Netherlands ranks 8th of 20 EU countries as an attractive market for opening a restaurant: start-up bureaucracy is low and Dutch people spend an average of around 2,100 euros per person per year on hospitality, more than 70 percent above Germans. The downside is staff shortages and high energy costs. A restaurant uses a lot of power for cooling, cooking, baking and ventilation, and at roughly 0.21 euro per kilowatt-hour the Netherlands sits clearly above Nordic markets at 0.09 to 0.13 euro. Utrecht emerges from the city comparison as the strongest Dutch location, Amsterdam mainly through purchasing power. For new businesses the margin is therefore less in the menu than in consumption per square metre.
nieuws.s109t: Net metering ends, EPV rates drop: 8 to 13 euros more rent per month
nieuws.s109p: The cabinet has sent the reduced energy performance fee to the Council of State. Without the change, tenants of a very energy-efficient home would pay 42 to 75 euros more per month once net metering ends on 1 January 2027; with the new rates that stays at 8 to 13 euros. The calculation is the same one hoteliers face: what is a self-generated kilowatt hour still worth when you can no longer offset it?
nieuws.s110t: Buying a heat pump this year earns 105 euros per kilowatt extra ISDE
nieuws.s110p: RVO has published the 2027 transition scheme. Buy the heat pump before 31 December 2026 and install it next year, and 225 euros of ISDE per kilowatt applies instead of 120 euros. The scheme opens on 5 January 2027 at 12.00, plus a 200 euro bonus for smart control via EEBus, S2 or Matter and a 250 euro label bonus for A+++. A smart 4 kilowatt air-to-water heat pump then reaches 1,955 euros. The amounts are not yet final.
nieuws.s111t: Enexis releases 195 megawatts, 2,500 applications can proceed
nieuws.s111p: Transport capacity becomes available at 101 of the 120 Enexis high-voltage substations, enough for around 2,500 applications: about 1,300 in the north with 98 megawatts and 1,200 in Brabant and Limburg with 97 megawatts. These are category 2 and 3 of ACM's prioritisation framework, vital functions and basic needs such as housing, care, education and childcare. Hotels generally fall outside those categories, so for their own connection or expansion little changes. A second release follows in 2027.
nieuws.s112t: TenneT pushes 30 percent more power through existing high-voltage lines
nieuws.s112p: TenneT is replacing the conductors on more than 800 kilometres of high-voltage line in the coming years. With the same towers and routes, 30 percent more power flows through. The 380 kilovolt link Krimpen aan den IJssel, Breukelen-Kortrijk and Diemen is due in spring 2027, Beverwijk-Oostzaan-Diemen follows in 2028. Dodewaard-Doetinchem and Maasbracht-Boxmeer-Dodewaard are on the list too. According to the national grid operator, capacity must at least double.
nieuws.s113t: ACM: without extra policy flexible capacity stays short, batteries are the bottleneck
nieuws.s113p: ACM has approved the first Dutch Flexibility Needs Assessment. Grid operators expect strong growth in battery storage, but whether market parties will actually make those investments is uncertain. Economic Affairs has six months to set a national flexibility target and can then design additional policy, for example a subsidy for non-fossil flexibility. For hotels with a battery or smart charging points, a new scheme could emerge on top of the existing business case.
nieuws.hn24t: Valk Exclusief Leeuwarden opens 100 new rooms
nieuws.hn24p: The first phase of the new wing at Valk Exclusief Hotel Leeuwarden is in use: 100 deluxe rooms, a guest lounge and rooms with floor-to-ceiling windows and a private balcony. A test room came first, used to refine layout, materials and comfort. Every extra room means more demand for hot water, cooling and lighting, and with a new wing the grid connection is usually the first hurdle.
nieuws.hn25t: Quality Lodgings adds eight hotels, including Hoog Holten
nieuws.hn25p: The collection of independent hotels grows by eight addresses in four countries: four in Germany, two in Italy, one in Belgium and Hotel Hoog Holten on the Sallandse Heuvelrug with 24 rooms and suites. Members stay independent but share visibility, knowledge and commercial cooperation. The network itself names that knowledge sharing as a reason to join, and energy purchasing is exactly the kind of topic where independent hotels are stronger together.
nieuws.s114t: Congestion measures are ready on paper, in practice little happens yet
nieuws.s114p: ACM has published the monitoring dashboard for congestion measures for the first time. Grid operators are on schedule with the preparations, but large-scale deployment is still absent, which the regulator does not consider alarming for the second quarter of 2026. More striking are the 2025 spending figures: 49 million euros on the high-voltage grids against 1.6 million euros at the regional operators combined. ACM is investigating that gap and will publish a new progress update in early 2027, the moment when the waiting list for a hotel expansion really has to start moving.
nieuws.s115t: Court of Appeal: an owners' association may commission a sustainability study first and decide on solar panels later
nieuws.s115p: A member of an owners' association (VvE) went to the court of appeal because the general meeting reserved 33,456 euros for a sustainability plan. The court ruled the vote was valid and that the VvE only has to weigh at the final investment decision whether solar panels still pay off now that net metering ends in 2027. That order, study first and investment later, also works for a hotel renovation: you pay for the plan once and do the maths with the tariffs in force at that moment.
nieuws.s116t: One small cable to the grid and the EIA for off-grid solar panels is gone
nieuws.s116p: The Dutch trade and industry appeal court ruled that a solar system with a battery is not entitled to the EIA code for installations that are not connected to the grid. The inverter turned out to be linked to the electricity grid by a small cable for stable operation, which makes the whole installation grid-connected. Of the 46 applications for that code in 2025, 5 were approved. For hotels with an island-mode or emergency power system it means: fully off the grid including the inverter, or a different code on the Energy List.
nieuws.s117t: Green roof with solar panels: vegetation trays burn through the entire roof build-up
nieuws.s117p: Peutz ran four fire tests on a simulated roof construction, commissioned by the government real estate agency. With solar panels on vegetation trays the fire spread to neighbouring panels and through the entire roof build-up within 14.5 minutes, reaching 150 degrees Celsius on the EPDM roofing and 196 degrees in the vegetation layer. With vegetation mats the fire stayed limited to the layer directly under the burning panel, with 20 to 25 degrees on the roofing. For hotels with a sedum roof and panels this touches fire compartmentation, and therefore the insurance file.
nieuws.hn26t: Parliament wants a simpler risk assessment, hospitality sector hopes for a 50 employee threshold
nieuws.hn26p: Parliament adopted four motions on 13 October to cut the administrative burden around the mandatory risk inventory and evaluation. One proposal is a single risk assessment for several similar locations, and KHN argues for an exemption threshold of 50 employees instead of 25, because in hospitality every part-timer and on-call worker counts. The motions are requests to the cabinet: current rules still apply and the cabinet has to come up with concrete measures by January 2027 at the latest.
nieuws.hn27t: Water becomes the next benchmark: 20 percent less consumption by 2035
nieuws.hn27p: The Dutch government wants large consumers to use twenty percent less water by 2035, which affects hotels through rooms, kitchen, sanitary facilities and wellness. Water utility WML is organising an inspiration session on 10 November at its water plant in Beegden about guest behaviour, climate and technical solutions, with a Green Key assessor at the table. Hot water is one of the largest consumption items in most hotels, so saving water almost always comes with a lower energy bill.
nieuws.s118t: Battery can move closer if you do the maths: tailor-made safety distances become the norm
nieuws.s118p: The ministry has published the results of the consultation on the amendment decree for energy storage systems, which drew 63 responses. The notification period for mobile batteries drops from four weeks to one week and should also apply to stationary systems, and a project-specific risk calculation using the RIVM method will soon be allowed for notifying systems as well, producing smaller distances than the fixed tables. For a hotel placing a battery next to the charging square or in the car park, that often saves metres and therefore permit room.
nieuws.s119t: Holland Solar wants 0 percent VAT on batteries and one system for solar, heat pump and car
nieuws.s119p: Ahead of the parliamentary round table on solar on roofs, Holland Solar asks the cabinet to scrap VAT on home batteries, resolve the double energy tax on storage and open local congestion markets to small consumers as well. According to the trade body extra generation alone is not enough: the Netherlands ended last year at 29.4 gigawatt peak, while the national energy system plan requires 3 to 4.4 gigawatt peak per year and RVO expects 1.3 gigawatt peak per year for the next three years. Interoperability should become a subsidy condition in the ISDE, so panels, battery and heat pump are steered as one system.
nieuws.s120t: NP RES: do not count on every roof, look at the car park too
nieuws.s120p: The national programme for regional energy strategies warns that the feasible roof potential is systematically overestimated: the easy roofs have been developed and around 45 percent of the potential on commercial roofs faces structural limitations. The SDE++ category for lightweight panels has existed since 2024 but is barely used, and the business case is under further pressure from the end of net metering and negative hourly prices. NP RES asks the cabinet for a national scheme for solar carports in car parks and for subsidy on solar power that first passes through a battery.
nieuws.s121t: From 2027 the feed-in tariff decides your yield, not the bare kWh price
nieuws.s121p: Once net metering stops on 1 January 2027, the feed-in tariff becomes the number that determines the energy bill of a solar roof, and the difference between suppliers runs into hundreds of euros a year. Anyone signing a two or three year contract now locks in that tariff for the whole term. In the same period the average all-in electricity price rose from around 0.25 to 0.29 euro per kilowatt hour and gas from 1.43 to 1.65 euro per cubic metre.
nieuws.s122t: Home battery stays outside the new battery rules, even at large capacity
nieuws.s122p: In the outline report of the consultation the ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management clarified that owners and installers of home batteries do not need to notify or apply for a permit under the amendment decree for energy storage systems, regardless of capacity. A home battery counts as a building services installation and therefore falls under the Buildings Decree, while the new PGS rules target commercial storage of large batteries. Of the 63 responses during the consultation, 52 were public, with more than 400 points raised.
nieuws.hn28t: 52 million overnight guests, and therefore more power per stay
nieuws.hn28p: The Netherlands Board of Tourism published its key figures for the hospitality economy this week: the country counted more than 52 million overnight guests in 2025, 22.3 million of them from abroad, almost 5 percent more than a year earlier. The economic significance of tourism and recreation came to 117.6 billion euros against 111.2 billion in 2024, good for 781,000 jobs. Important with those figures: this is total economic significance under the Tourism Satellite Account, not hotel revenue, and every extra overnight stay does add to electricity, hot water and cooling use.
nieuws.hn29t: Belgium considers 21 percent VAT on accommodation, the Netherlands went first
nieuws.hn29p: Leaked Belgian government plans put VAT on accommodation for hotels, holiday homes and campsites at 21 percent, while it has already been at 12 percent since March 2026. The Netherlands raised the rate for accommodation from 9 to 21 percent on 1 January 2026, with campsites staying at 9 percent, and the evaluation still has to follow. Germany charges 7 percent and France 10 percent, which makes the Dutch position in border regions expensive for hotel stays.
nieuws.s123t: Energy sharing becomes mandatory in 2027, the administration stays the bottleneck
nieuws.s123p: From the first half of 2027 suppliers must offer energy sharing between customers of different suppliers; today it is already possible within one supplier, through feed-in aggregation or peer-to-peer trading. Only power fed in and taken off in the same quarter hour counts as shared, and the electricity still runs over the same grid: it is mainly registration and settlement, with energy tax on the shared part. Grid operator costs end up in the tariffs everyone pays, supplier costs are paid by the participants themselves. For a hotel with a neighbouring building or a sister location it is an alternative to feeding back at a low rate, as long as sharer and receiver really overlap quarter by quarter.
nieuws.s124t: Waiting list for extra power keeps growing, flexible contracts surge
nieuws.s124p: The waiting list for consumption at the regional grid operators rose in the first half of 2026 from 15,154 to 15,498 applications and from 9,305 to 9,986 megawatts, while TenneT falls slightly for the first time in years to 205 applications and 34.2 gigawatts. Capacity limitation contracts on feed-in grew in six months from 238 contracts and 848.7 megawatts to 394 contracts and 2,885.7 megawatts, and block power, mainly used for charging vehicle fleets, from 142 to 212 contracts. Applications with social priority, including batteries, already exceed the level of all of 2025 in half a year. The average connection time for small consumers stays at 45 weeks.
nieuws.s125t: SDE++ period ends: the number of subsidised solar projects shrinks faster
nieuws.s125p: For a growing number of solar installations the fifteen-year subsidy period is ending, and that shows in the VertiCer register: in the third quarter of 2026 a net 630 installations disappeared, against 374 in the second and 230 in the first quarter. Over the first nine months the count stands at 1,234 installations and 1,101.5 megawatt peak less, more than six times the decline of all 2025. Some 35,048 projects remain in the register, of which 8,456 small installations that will largely expire in the next two years. For a hotel with SDE++ on the roof this is the moment to recalculate the business case after subsidy, with self-consumption and storage instead of feed-in.
nieuws.hn30t: Utrecht raises tourist tax to 12.5 percent, hotels send an urgent letter
nieuws.hn30p: In Utrecht's coalition agreement the tourist tax rises by 25 percent in 2027 to 12.5 percent, good for an estimated 1.7 million euros extra. Hoteliers sent an urgent letter and point to a leakage effect towards other municipalities, after the VAT increase from 9 to 21 percent earlier this year. According to analyst Henri-Dick Rondhuis of MinersRepublic, Amsterdam hotels already absorb a large part of the increase in their margin, and that margin is thin. The city council debates the budget at the end of October, with the final debate scheduled for 12 November.
nieuws.hn31t: Reclaiming VAT on accommodation: what foreign business guests can and cannot do
nieuws.hn31p: Since 1 January 2026 VAT on hotel stays is 21 percent, and KHN lists the rules for reclaiming it. For accommodation and restaurant services there is no VAT reverse charge, so foreign guests cannot reclaim that VAT, also not through the export refund scheme, which only covers goods. Dutch business guests offset the VAT in their own return, and reverse charging only applies in certain cases for meeting facilities and room hire in a business context. Communicating this clearly at the front desk prevents debates and incorrect expectations on the invoice.
nieuws.s126t: Battery rules now cover only lithium and sodium, redox-flow gets its own route
nieuws.s126p: The ministry narrows the scope of the energy storage amendment to lithium and sodium batteries, which leaves redox-flow and lead batteries outside PGS 37. For redox-flow the general duty of care applies, plus a risk calculation through module 1 of the environmental safety method, and for lead batteries and other energy carriers where a thermal chain reaction cannot occur based on the chemistry the ministry chooses a lighter route. Sodium-ion does fall under the rules, because a self-reinforcing temperature rise is possible there too. For a hotel placing a battery next to the charging square or on the car park, the chemistry now determines which rules and which distances apply.
nieuws.s127t: NPE 2026 is a guiding path, not a blueprint
nieuws.s127p: Minister Stientje van Veldhoven writes to parliament that the revised National Energy System Plan is not a blueprint but a guiding path to 2040. The standing committee for Climate and Green Growth submitted 122 questions, among them on power demand and system costs in the plan presented on Budget Day. Along that development path import dependence falls from about 80 percent today to about 50 percent in 2040, in line with the European climate target for that year. For hotels that means no fixed energy mix, but a framework within which grid capacity, storage and electrification are allocated.
nieuws.s128t: Brussels works on a real energy union against high energy costs
nieuws.s128p: Commission president Ursula von der Leyen announced a package in the European Parliament that should appear in December and must counter critical dependence on a single supplier. According to her the problem has two sides: too much dependence on foreign fossil fuels, with gas setting the price, and the absence of a real European energy union. She mentions better use of grids and interconnectors and joint purchasing power; on the European grid package member states already agreed their position in June. The energy sanctions against Russia remain in force until the war stops.
nieuws.s129t: Consumers association wants 10 cents per fed-in kWh as successor to net metering
nieuws.s129p: Ahead of the round table on solar on roofs in parliament, the Consumers Association asks that solar panels remain attractive for tenants and homeowners after 1 January 2027. More than 1 in 3 Dutch homes has panels, but most of those households benefit only partly from the output, because the power is not used at the moment of generation. The alternative the association worked out two years ago is a solar subsidy of 10 euro cents per kilowatt hour fed back for a fixed period of 15 years. The same calculation applies to hotels with a large roof and little own consumption during the day.
nieuws.s130t: TU Delft looks for batteries without lithium, NWO grants 850,000 euros
nieuws.s130p: Battery researcher Xuehang Wang of TU Delft receives a Vidi grant of up to 850,000 euros to improve batteries based on polymers, using ions other than lithium. Lithium is a critical raw material with limited availability, while polymers and sodium are abundant, which fits the European goals of becoming less dependent on raw materials. NWO previously funded three projects on circular batteries, including sodium-ion at the University of Twente. For the business case of a battery behind the meter this says something about the direction of the technology, not about what is available this year.
nieuws.hn32t: Fletcher Hotels passes into the hands of Sunday PropTech
nieuws.hn32p: Sunday PropTech acquires 100 percent of Fletcher Hotels from Egeria and Fletcher's management. With 170 hotels, 130 owned and 40 partner hotels in the Netherlands, Germany and Belgium, Fletcher is the largest hotel group in the country, with around 5,800 employees and mainly three and four star hotels. The buyer names technology, brand building and asset management as priorities and wants to invest in the organisation and in the hotels; Rothschild & Co advised on the transaction, which still has to close under the usual conditions. With 170 locations, energy procurement is one of the largest costs a new owner can address jointly.
nieuws.hn33t: KHN: what is your plan if the power is out for 72 hours?
nieuws.hn33p: KHN points to the government's Denk vooruit campaign and asks hospitality entrepreneurs to think about long power outages, a cyber attack or a failing water supply. The campaign includes a toolkit and a playbook that helps you map which parts of your business are essential and which suppliers you depend on. The advice is to work through what 72 hours without power, water, internet or telephony means for guests, kitchen equipment, stock and payments, and to record who does what. For hotels with cold storage, lift systems and digital room doors that is not a theoretical scenario.
